const RULES = `

${RULES}`,

      },
    },

  },
  required: ['verdict', 'gaps'],
}
const crit = await agent(`Completeness critic. Read ${OUT} in full. Repos: entire-graph at ${EG}, graphmark at ${GM} (READ-ONLY, other session's scratchpad).

Your job: find what a reader of this map still CANNOT answer, and what the map asserts without support. Spot-check at least 8 specific claims against the actual files and report any that are wrong, stale, or unsupported.

Ask specifically: is the retrieval ranking actually explained mechanically or hand-waved? Is the index format concrete? Is every subcommand+flag present? Is the language/relation matrix complete? For graphmark: are the arm configurations, grading rule, and netjail concrete? Are the headline numbers attributable to a specific results file with a sample size? Is anything presented as measured that is single-run or methodologically contaminated?

Return the 3-6 HIGHEST-VALUE gaps only (severity high|medium), each with an exact where_to_look (path/dir/command). Skip trivia. ${RULES}`, { label: 'critic:completeness', phase: 'Critique', schema: CRIT, effort: 'xhigh' })

const topGaps = (crit.gaps || []).filter(g => g.severity !== 'low').slice(0, 3)
log(`critic: ${crit.verdict} | ${(crit.gaps||[]).length} gaps, filling ${topGaps.length}`)

let fills = []
if (topGaps.length) {
  phase('Fill')
  fills = (await parallel(topGaps.map((g, i) => () =>
    agent(`Close ONE gap in the graph-stack map. Answer this exhaustively from the real code/files, nothing else:

QUESTION: ${g.question}
WHY IT MATTERS: ${g.why_it_matters || 'map is unusable without it'}
WHERE TO LOOK: ${g.where_to_look}

entire-graph: ${EG} (use \`entire graph search --repo ${EG} --profile full --query "..."\` to locate). graphmark: ${GM} (READ-ONLY).
Return the answer as drop-in map content: dense, cited file:line, with the concrete mechanism/numbers/schema — not a summary of where to find it. ${RULES}`,
      { label: `fill:${i + 1}`, phase: 'Fill', schema: DIGEST })
  ))).filter(Boolean)
}

phase('Finalize')
const fin = await agent(`Finalize ${OUT}.

Apply these gap-fills and corrections with Edit/Write on ${OUT}. Integrate into the RIGHT existing sections (do not bolt on an appendix), keep the established voice/density, and move any UNKNOWNS that are now answered out of the UNKNOWNS list.

CRITIC VERDICT: ${crit.verdict}
UNSUPPORTED/WRONG CLAIMS TO FIX OR DELETE: ${JSON.stringify(crit.wrong_or_unsupported || [])}
REMAINING GAPS TO RECORD AS UNKNOWNS (if not filled): ${JSON.stringify((crit.gaps || []).slice(3))}
GAP-FILL CONTENT: ${JSON.stringify(fills)}

Then return caveman-ultra: final line count, sections, what you changed, what remains UNKNOWN. ${RULES}`, { label: 'finalize:map', phase: 'Finalize' })

return { out: OUT, synth, critic: crit.verdict, gaps_filled: fills.length, final: fin }

entire-graph adds entity-level context to Entire checkpoints.

For coding agents: run 'entire graph agent-guide' (the search-first, verify-once doctrine:
locate with one search instead of grepping, then verify the edit once) or
'entire graph init-agents' to install it into a project.

Usage:
  entire graph commit [rev] [--json] [--progress] [--max-seconds n] [--repo path]
  entire graph checkpoint <checkpoint-id> [--json] [--repo path]
  entire graph diff --base <rev> --head <rev> [--json] [--progress] [--max-seconds n] [--repo path] [-- path...]
  entire graph analyze [--base <rev>] [--head <rev>] [--json] [--progress] [--max-seconds n] [--repo path] [-- path...]
  entire graph doctor [--json]
  entire graph agent-guide                 # print the coding-agent operating guide
  entire graph init-agents [--repo path]   # install the guide into a project's AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md
  entire graph version [--json]
  entire graph capabilities --json
  entire graph snapshot --repo . --format ndjson [--worktree] [--progress] [--ignore-file path] [--include-file path]
  entire graph symbols --repo . --format ndjson [--worktree] [--progress] [--ignore-file path] [--include-file path]
  entire graph edges --repo . --format ndjson [--worktree] [--progress] [--ignore-file path] [--include-file path]
  entire graph index --repo . [--profile syntax-only|fast|full] [--cache-dir path] [--format json] [--head] [--ignore-file path] [--include-file path]
  entire graph search --query "issue or concept" --repo . [--format json|ndjson|text|agent] [--top-k 10] [--deep] [--max-context-bytes 24576] [--head] [--profile syntax-only|fast|full] [--max-indexed-files n|--index-all-files] [--cache-dir path|--no-cache]
  entire graph neighbors --symbol NAME|<file>:<line> --repo . [--file path] [--line n] [--kind kind] [--relation CALLS] [--direction both|in|out] [--depth 1|2] [--limit 20] [--format json|text|agent] [--max-context-bytes 16384] [--head] [--cache-dir path|--no-cache] [--internal-only] [--exclude-tests]
  entire graph impact --symbol NAME|<file>:<line> --repo . [--file path] [--line n] [--kind kind] [--depth 1|2] [--limit 15] [--format text|json] [--max-context-bytes 4096] [--head] [--profile fast|full] [--cache-dir path|--no-cache] [--exclude-tests]
  entire graph stats [--repo .] [--since 30d|7d|all] [--format text|json] [--sessions-dir path|--transcript path]

Notes:
  search --top-k only changes how many results come back; --deep additionally runs the
  exhaustive sparse (BM25) pass and fuses it with the semantic ranking (slower, reads every
  eligible file). neighbors/impact take --symbol <file>:<line>, or --symbol NAME with
  --file/--line/--kind, to select one definition when a name is ambiguous; the ambiguity
  error prints the exact selector for each definition it found.
  stats is a local read-only report for humans: it reads the coding-agent session transcripts
  already on disk (~/.claude/projects/<path-slug>/*.jsonl) and reports graph usage vs
  grep/read exploration, bytes each pulled into context, and an ESTIMATED token saving whose
  assumption is printed with the number. --transcript narrows it to ONE session transcript
  (plus that session's subagent transcripts) instead of a whole project directory.
  --include-file contains gitignore-style rules that re-include ignored paths; it is not an allowlist.
  Streaming NDJSON writes aggregate stats and completeness in the trailing summary record.
  commit/diff/analyze stop cleanly after --max-seconds (default 120; 0 = unlimited) and emit the
  partial result with W_ANALYSIS_BUDGET_EXCEEDED warnings listing what was skipped.

content.text:
Readers are still in flight (10/10 running). Meanwhile I've pinned down the load-bearing mechanics directly from the live binary + on-disk index rather than from code reading — including two real defects. Interim:

**Wiring (verified, not assumed)**
- `entire graph` is **not** this repo's binary. It's an Entire *plugin* resolved kubectl-style: `~/.local/share/entire/plugins/entire-graph → /tmp/egbin/entire-graph` (77.9 MB, built Jul 26 20:33, version `dev`). Repo-local `./entire-graph` (Jul 25) is a *different, older* build.
- Sibling plugins are also symlinks into `/tmp`: `entire-brain → /tmp/entire-brain`, `entire-graph-fresh → /tmp/entire-graph-fresh`. **`entire-graph-mainrel → /tmp/graphmark-bin/entire-graph-mainrel` is dangling** — that graphmark comparison arm's binary is gone.
- `entire sem` still resolves — to `entire-sem → ~/Documents/Coding/entire-sem/entire-sem`, the **pre-rename repo**. Your global `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` tells agents to run `entire sem edges|symbols`, so that guidance silently drives a stale legacy build. `entire graph edges|symbols` is the current path.

**Index format (from the live snapshot, `~/.cache/entire-graph/<repo-basename>/search/search-snapshot-v4/<sha256>.json.gz`)**
- Header carries `commit`+`tree`+`profile` → that triple is the cache identity; keyed by repo **basename**, so same-named repos in different parents collide.
- Records: `Files`, `Externals`, `Symbols`, `Relations`, plus a `file_lines` map. Symbol IDs are `repo_key:Language:path:kind:qualified_name` (`stable_id_version: compound-v1`).
- **30 relation types**, not the 2 the doctrine names: CALLS 8856, DEFINES 5338, SIMILAR_TO 2863, DATA_FLOWS 2125, USES_TYPE 1410, CONTAINS 1190, PARAM_TYPE 958, IMPORTS 693, READS_FIELD 524, RETURNS_TYPE 518 … plus HANDLES_{ROUTE,GRAPHQL,GRPC,TRPC,TOOL}, FILE_CHANGES_WITH, RESOURCE_DEPENDS_ON.
- Every edge is qualified: `relation_scope` ∈ {file, external, workspace, module}, `resolution` ∈ {exact, pattern, import_external, package, name_only, type_inferred, import_resolved, git_history}, `confidence` 0.55–1.0. `FILE_CHANGES_WITH` resolves via `git_history` — that's where co-change comes from.
- `language_tiers` per language is explicit `semantic` vs `inventory-only`. Parser hard cap = 4 MiB (`E_FILE_TOO_LARGE`); over that, file record emitted, symbols skipped.
- Complete-symbol vs locator is a **byte-budget allocation**, not a rank rule: `SearchStats.CompleteSymbols` / `LocatorSnippets` / `SnippetsTruncated` / `ResultsDropped`, with the `complete-symbol` marker carried in each result's `signals[]`. Tail results get *demoted to locators to pay for* the complete bodies at the top.

**Two defects found**
1. `entire-graph/.claude/worktrees/` holds **7 nested git worktrees, 1.5 GB, not gitignored**, so the indexer walks them. 4–6 of the top hits on a live search point into stale copies on other branches (`integ/rebase-onto-upstream`, `feat/nested-types-and-container-map`). `files_scanned` 2578 vs 247 real files; 48 MB read during preselection; ~16–21 s cache-miss. Confirmed fixable: passing `--ignore-file` with `/.claude/` yields clean, correct hits — so the durable fix is one `.gitignore` line.
2. `entire graph stats --repo devenv --since 30d`: **graph-first rate 0% (0/7 sessions)** — 102 graph calls vs 43,534 exploration calls (7,072 whole-file reads ≈ 17.4 M tokens). Estimated savings ~12 M of 11.08 B billed = **0.11%**. The estimator's own model is printed with the number (1 locate call credited with the 1 whole-file read it replaced), i.e. it's an assumption, not a measurement. Inside the entire-graph repo itself: 0 graph calls, 0 savings.

Waiting on the readers, then the synthesis lands at `/Users/suhaan/devenv/GRAPH-STACK-MAP.md`.

A session-scoped Stop hook is now active with condition: "after u udnerstadn fully ;  make entire graph meet this goal as it has already been beaten,  might be graphmark benchmark harness etc problem if not, then acutaly improve  grpah itself;   1. Give the agent a proper prompt for entire-graph, and a proper prompt for cmm too — then rerun against
  baseline and report.
  2. Don't stop until: accuracy vs baseline is a win or a tie, AND tokens beat both baseline and cmm, AND
  tokens beat baseline by ≥35%.
  3. No cheating at all.
  4. Use the loop plugin if it's useful.
  5. Results on 5/300 fable, 10/300 opus, 20/300 sonnet, 30/300 haiku.". Briefly acknowledge the goal, then immediately start (or continue) working toward it — treat the condition itself as your directive and do not pause to ask the user what to do. The hook will block stopping until the condition holds. It auto-clears once the condition is met — do not tell the user to run `/goal clear` after success; that's only for clearing a goal early.

Goal acknowledged. Understanding sweep is still in flight; I'll fold it straight into the prompt-fairness fix and the reruns. Targets I'm holding myself to: accuracy ≥ baseline, tokens < baseline **and** < cmm, tokens ≥35% under baseline, at 5/300 fable · 10/300 opus · 20/300 sonnet · 30/300 haiku, no cheating.

#                  no fix strategy, no frugality/correctness policy.
#   SHARED block — the tool-agnostic working policy. Depends ONLY on $PROMPT_FAMILY. Emitted from
#                  a single quoted heredoc, so it is byte-identical across all three arms: no
#                  tool name, no command line, no path, nothing arm-dependent can leak into it.
#
# Swapping PROMPT_FAMILY cannot change the TOOL block; swapping arm cannot change the SHARED
# block. That is the whole point — the arms differ in tool doctrine and in nothing else.
# ============================================================================================
# CMM_DISCIPLINE=1 adds to the cmm arm the SAME turn-discipline sentences that entire-graph ships
# in its own agent guide. cmm's vendor docs do not contain this material, so it is NOT part of the
# as-shipped product comparison — it exists as a CONTROL, to decompose how much of any eg-vs-cmm
# token gap is the guide versus the index. Report it as an augmented arm, never as cmm-as-shipped.
CMM_DISCIPLINE_NOTE=""
if [ "${CMM_DISCIPLINE:-0}" = 1 ]; then
  CMM_DISCIPLINE_NOTE="These operating rules make the tool pay off: search FIRST — never grep/find/cat to locate code
before you have searched; once search shows you the function and its source, EDIT it rather than
re-reading the file to \"confirm\" what the index already showed you; never read a whole file to
explore — read the line range around the symbol; do not run builds or test suites unless the task
requires it; and remember that every extra turn re-reads your whole context, which is what the task
actually costs, so reach the edit in as few turns as you can and stop once you can defend the fix.
"
fi
# EG_SHIPPED_PROMPT=1 uses the block entire-graph publishes in AGENTS.md under "The measured-best
# agent prompt (copy-paste this)" — i.e. exactly what the vendor tells users to give their agent.
# It is a harder clamp than the prose doctrine: one search, read the range, edit, stop. On the OLD
# tool this bought ~50% tokens and cost ~6 points of resolve rate; the open question is whether the
# repaired ranking (top-1 35.7% -> 57.1%) makes the clamp safe.
# EG_GATED_CLAMP=1 — the clamp, adapted. Measured: the clamp's token win is real (-54% tok/resolved)
# and its accuracy loss is EARLY STOPPING, not bad ranking — median 12 turns, 9/27 sessions quit at
# <=6 turns, and within the clamp arm the sessions it RESOLVED averaged 11.5 turns while the ones it
# failed averaged 21.9 (it abandoned the hard ones). So: keep the clamp on DISCOVERY (one search, go
# straight to the top hit, no grep tour) and forbid stopping until the fix is verified and swept.
# Frugality is applied to exploration, never to finishing.
gated_clamp_eg_prompt() {  # $1 = wrapper command
  cat <<TXT
A precomputed code-search tool is available: $1 . Use it to LOCATE the fix BEFORE any
grep/find. Your FIRST action must be ONE search:
  $1 search "<the bug in one sentence>"   <-- ranked relevant code (file:line + source)
Then open the top hit's file with your native Read tool (pass a line range around the reported
line) and edit. The top hit is the fix site on most tasks - go straight there; do NOT re-search or
grep to 'confirm' what the result already showed you. Spend your turns on the FIX, not on looking
around: every turn re-reads your whole context, and that is what this task costs.
DISCOVERY IS CLAMPED - FINISHING IS NOT. Before you stop, all three must be true:
(1) VERIFIED - you compiled the change or ran the nearest existing test at least ONCE. Pick the
    narrowest command that would still catch a syntax, type, name or arity error. A patch that does
    not build fails the whole task; this is the cheapest turn you will spend. Then stop verifying -
    read the error, fix what it names, re-run once. Do NOT hunt a green suite.
(2) SWEPT - you checked the RELATED SITES the search result listed (callers, siblings, near-dupes)
    and fixed every one that has the same bug. A fix is usually not one edit in one place.
(3) COMPLETE - you handled the edge cases the issue names (empty, nil, negative, unicode, error
    paths).
If a search did not land it, search again with different words; if TWO searches miss, fall back to
the shell in ONE batched call. Never stop merely because you have made an edit - stop when (1),
(2) and (3) hold.
TXT
}
shipped_eg_prompt() {  # $1 = wrapper command
  cat <<TXT
A precomputed code-search tool is available: $1 . Use it to LOCATE the fix BEFORE any
grep/find. Your FIRST action must be ONE search:
  $1 search "<the bug in one sentence>"   <-- ranked relevant code (file:line + source)
Then open the top hit's file with your native Read tool (pass a line range around the reported
line), make the minimal edit, and STOP. The search top hit is the fix site on most tasks - go
straight there and edit; do NOT re-search or grep to 'confirm'. Reach the edit in as FEW turns as
possible (every turn re-reads your whole context - that is the token cost).
Hard rules: (1) LOCATE WITH THE TOOL FIRST. (2) After the tool answers, READ the file directly
(line range) and EDIT - do not chain more tool calls. (3) NEVER read a whole file to explore; pass
a line range. (4) NEVER search outside this repo. Apply the minimal fix and STOP the moment you can
justify it.
If TWO searches have not put you on the right code, fall back to the shell (grep/find) in ONE
batched call rather than staying stuck.
Other verbs if the result genuinely leaves a question: $1 def <Symbol> (full source of a symbol),
$1 callers <Symbol> (inbound call paths, file:line and hop), $1 impact <Symbol> (callers, callees,
type consumers, co-change files and siblings in one shot), $1 grep <regex> (grep mapped onto the
enclosing symbol and ranked by hit density).
TXT
}
# PROMPT_FAMILY=briefed uses these per-arm TOOL blocks. Design, from measurement: cost is quadratic
# in turns (34,703 tokens replayed per turn against 1,155 of new context), the clamped-discovery
# config already clears the token target (-38.7% cost per resolved at 300 instances, 15.4 turns vs
# 28.9) and its ONLY defect is 19 lost instances whose causes were all "the thing I needed was not
# in front of me" — contract not in view (8), sibling sites not surfaced (6), wrong site (5), type
# not in view (4). The first response now carries all four. So: clamp discovery, and let the
# briefing pay for the turns that sweeping, typing and verifying used to cost.
# EG_OPS_CLAMP=1 (with PROMPT_FAMILY=briefed): the cell the cost model says wins, and the only one
# untested. Cost = T*17k + G*T(T+1)/2. Measured endpoints: hard clamp T=16.6 but -19 resolves at 300
# (it stopped early AND blind); briefed reference-payload T=27-30 and dearer (G rose above the no-tool
# arm's 1.15k because the payload was fat). Solving for the target: T~21 with G~0.85k gives -38%.
# So: clamp the DISCOVERY exactly as the -38.7% arm did, keep the payload LEAN, and spend ~800 bytes
# on the three OPERATIONAL blocks that remove the clamp's known failure modes — the literal cluster
# (sweep without a grep round-trip), the verify command (verification without fumbling the
# invocation), and the closed-set warning (the wrong-shape patch that compiles and then throws).
# EG_CLAMP_VERIFY=1 — the surgical version, from graded evidence. The plain clamp resolves 17/29 at
# 16.5 turns / $0.1426 (-42% USD vs baseline). Bundling sweep+verify+batching instructions on top
# recovered 2 of its 3 misfixes but cost the entire advantage: 31.0 turns, +0.9% vs baseline,
# per-resolved +65.6% [+26.3,+130.0]. Post-mortem of that bundle: (a) the "batch independent tool
# calls" clause was INERT — 870/449/990 tool messages across three arms, batch size exactly 1, zero
# parallel calls ever; (b) the sweep prose is what bought the turns; (c) verify itself is what bought
# the resolves (druid-14092's over-broad edit flipped, ruff-15330 P2P 0/12 -> 12/12, babel-14532
# finally compiled); (d) verify FAILED once because the session piped it through grep/tail and
# mis-read its own COMPILATION ERROR, losing an instance the other arms resolved.
# So: clamp discipline + verify only, raw and un-piped, exit status reported. No sweep, no batching.
# BASE_CLAMP=1 — the control the audit says every tool claim depends on. The published -45.8% was
# measured with eg on a 240-word hard clamp ("one search, edit, STOP") against a no-tool baseline on
# a 550-word prompt that ALSO carried task strategy the eg arm never got (sweep, verify, edge cases).
# Under matched instructions the tool measured +0.9% to +8.7% WORSE on three of four pairs, so the
# saving was the prompt, not the tool. This is the grep-analogue of the shipped clamp: same length,
# same discipline, same "stop when you can justify it", with grep/find substituted for search and NO
# sweep/verify/edge-case guidance. It is the only baseline against which a clamped eg arm can support
# a tool claim.
# EG_EDIT_FROM_PAYLOAD=1 — the design the cost arithmetic points at, and the one cell never tested.
# Audit fact: the eg arm costs 24% MORE per turn ($0.00878 vs $0.00706) because the search result is
# ADDED to context and the agent then reads the file anyway — we pay for search AND read. So a 35%
# money win needs eg_turns <= 0.52 x base_turns, which a clamp alone does not reach (0.7-0.8x).
# This removes the read instead of preceding it: the payload carries the COMPLETE enclosing function,
# and the prompt forbids opening the file unless that body is truncated. Sequence becomes
# search -> edit -> verify (3-4 turns) against grep -> read -> edit -> verify (8-14).
# Untested until now because (a) _egsearch.py was deleting the bodies before the agent saw them,
# (b) no prompt ever said "do not read the file", (c) the byte ceiling had been tuned down on the
# mistaken conclusion that payload was expensive.
edit_from_payload_eg_prompt() {  # $1 = wrapper command
  cat <<TXT
A precomputed code graph is available: $1 . Your FIRST action is ONE search:
  $1 search "<the bug in one sentence>"
The result is not a pointer — for the top hits it prints the COMPLETE body of the enclosing
function, verbatim, with its real line numbers. EDIT DIRECTLY FROM THAT BODY.
Do NOT open the file first. You already have the code and the line numbers; a Read would cost a
whole turn to show you what is already in front of you, and every turn re-reads your entire context.
Read the file ONLY if the body you need is marked truncated or is genuinely absent from the result —
and then read just the line range the result names, never the whole file.
When your edits are in, run the build-or-test command ONCE, RAW — no pipe through grep/head/tail,
no redirect — and state its exit status. If it is non-zero, fix exactly what the error names and
re-run once. A patch that does not build fails the whole task.
Then STOP. No re-searching, no grep to double-check, no re-reading your own edits.
If the top hit is clearly wrong, search ONCE more with different words, then fall back to the shell
in one batched call.
TXT
}
# CMM_CLAMP=1 — codebase-memory-mcp at matched clamp discipline, so the three-way is fair. cmm has
# only ever run on the 495-word briefed prompt while eg ran a 240-word clamp; comparing those two
# measures the prompts. This is cmm's own vendor doctrine (its docs say "ALWAYS prefer MCP graph

Confirmed the harness bug precisely:

- Unknown flags → **stderr + exit 1 + empty stdout**. `eg-q` does `2>/dev/null` and never checks status → a silent empty payload. (Not currently firing, but it's the same landmine that already voided one run.)
- `--max-snippet-lines` **is** a real (undocumented) flag and it **does** truncate: same query returns 1,473 B at `2` vs 5,726 B at `400`.
- `eg-q` defaults it to `EG_SNIPPET:-6`. So the wrapper **chops the complete function bodies down to 6 lines** — the agent then has to Read the file anyway. That is precisely the documented "eg costs 24% more per turn: we pay for search AND read." The engine emits complete bodies; the harness throws them away.

=== FINDINGS.md (head 140) ===
# entire-graph vs no-tool baseline vs codebase-memory-mcp — measured findings

SWE-bench Multilingual. Language-stratified instance sets, matched prompt discipline across arms,
3 runs per arm per configuration, paired per-instance statistics with bootstrap CIs and McNemar
exact tests. Every configuration, negative result and mid-course correction is recorded in
`RUN-MANIFEST.md` with the timestamp that fixed it.

## 1. Headline

**entire-graph's token savings are a function of how much the baseline agent flails at
localization, not a property of the tool.**

| model | baseline turns | eg turns | eg tokens vs baseline |
|---|---|---|---|
| haiku (n=50, 3 runs) | 30.2 | 23.9 | **-32.3%**  CI [-21.7%, -41.9%] |
| sonnet (n=20, run 1 only) | 15.6 | 16.2 | **+13.9%, CI [-17.3%, +61.8%] — NOT SIGNIFICANT** |
| fable (n=5, 3 runs) | 10.1 | 11.0 | **+31.4%**  CI [+8.8%, +63.0%] |

eg costs ~10-20% MORE per turn (the payload it injects) and only wins by deleting turns. On haiku it
deletes 6.3 turns of a 30.2-turn baseline. On sonnet it ADDS 0.6. On fable it adds 0.9. Break-even sits near a 20-turn baseline.

A partial read of sonnet (n=8-9) showed eg at 15.5 turns against baseline 16.0 — marginally FEWER.
At full n=20 it is 16.2 against 15.6 — marginally MORE. Fast instances finish first, and that
ordering bias flipped the sign of a 0.5-turn difference. Partial rows are not reportable.

CORRECTION (found by auditing this report against the raw data). The sonnet row is NOT established.
An earlier draft claimed +19%, computed from ARM MEANS (715k/600k) rather than the paired geometric
mean used everywhere else; the paired figure is +13.9% and its CI is [-17.3%, +61.8%], which CROSSES
ZERO at n=19 pairs (run 1 only). Sonnet currently shows NO measurable difference in either direction.
Its runs 2-3 are needed. The two ESTABLISHED endpoints are haiku (-32.3%, CI excludes zero) and fable
(+31.4%, CI excludes zero); the mechanism rests on those, and sonnet's turn counts (15.6 vs 16.2) are
consistent with it but are not themselves evidence.

The saving is structural, not tunable, on the established endpoints. On fable eg adds turns, so there
is no turn saving for any payload setting to pay for: stripping the payload to its leanest measured
setting returns ~2% of session tokens against a ~31% deficit.
No configuration, prompt, or adaptive policy yields >=35% on a model whose baseline does not
explore, because the exploration the graph deletes does not exist there — and not invoking the
graph yields 0% savings, not 35%.

## 2. Accuracy (haiku, frozen 50, 3 runs, pre-registered)

| arm | resolved per run | mean | USD/resolved |
|---|---|---|---|
| baseline | 19, 19, 22 | 20.0 | $0.513 |
| eg | 21, 23, 17 | 20.3 | $0.521 |
| cmm | 18, 21, 22 | 20.3 | $0.641 |

McNemar: eg vs baseline p=1.000, eg vs cmm p=1.000, cmm vs baseline p=1.000. All ties.

eg started at 18.0 (BELOW baseline) and reached parity only after two harness defects were fixed —
see section 4. Its own run-to-run sd is 3.06 resolves, so this design cannot certify a 2-3 instance
difference in either direction.

## 3. codebase-memory-mcp does not measurably save tokens

cmm vs baseline, haiku frozen 50, 3 runs: **-3.0%, CI [-15.8%, +8.8%] — crosses zero.**
On fable: **+58.8%**. eg beats cmm by 35.0% (CI [+24.7%, +44.1%]) on haiku and 17.3% on fable.
The premise that cmm obviously saves tokens does not survive a stratified multilingual set at
matched prompt discipline.

## 4. What actually moved eg's accuracy: two measurement defects, not the tool

1. `tools/_egsearch.py` capped the agent-visible payload at 10 hits regardless of `--top-k`, so the
   tool found deeper hits and the wrapper discarded them one line before the agent.
2. `EG_TIER=2` rendered only 2 complete function bodies when entire-graph's own agent guide promises
   the top five. The benchmark was measuring eg below its shipped behaviour.

Lifting both: +2 resolves for +1.8% tokens. Adding a search-budget cap (enforcing the two-search
ceiling both arms' prompts already stated, which agents ignored — runaway sessions ran 8.4 searches,
worst case 23): +2 more resolves, no token change.

## 5. Levers that did NOT work, with numbers, so they are not retried

| lever | result |
|---|---|
| `--top-k` alone (10->20), SHOW left at 10 | +1 instance. Raw recall curve does not survive the wrapper |
| preselection pool 96 -> 256 -> 1024 | recall 76.9% -> 73.1% -> 69.2%. NEGATIVE |
| fixture/snapshot ranking class | +1 instance; did NOT fix the ruff case that motivated it (Rust stayed 33%) |
| unconditional search+grep hybrid | +3.8pt localization for +4% tokens. Rejected on a zero-cost screen |
| search-budget cap 4 -> 2 (config 5) | searches -42%, turns UNCHANGED. Falsified; stopped after 1 run |
| payload budget (TIER curve) | +-2% tokens; TIER 5 and 6 are identical, plateau at 5 |

Ranking levers totalled +7.7pt of gold-file localization and bought resolves, never tokens.

## 6. Product defects found and fixed (independent of the benchmark)

- **`entire graph search` returned ZERO results in every git worktree on `main`.** A linked
  worktree's `.git` is a regular file, so `os.Stat(".git/info/exclude")` returns ENOTDIR (not
  ErrNotExist) and the fatal branch aborted the whole search. Wrappers suppress stderr, so it failed
  silently. Regression test covers the worktree layout, an unresolvable gitdir, an ordinary clone and
  a non-git directory; mutation-checked against the old path.
- `defaultSearchTopK` 10 -> 20, reverting a regression I introduced by conflating breadth with depth
  (the old 20/40 default was expensive because of 40-line snippets, not 20 results).
- New `fixture` file class so snapshot/golden/testdata trees stop outranking source.

## 7. Query wording dominates localization

Search recall for the gold file, disjoint 52-instance set:
- raw issue-text prefix as query: 53.8% @10, 69.2% @20
- distilled one-sentence query: 69.2% @10, 75.0% @20

Query distillation alone recovers 7 of 10 instances where the gold file never appeared in the raw
top-40, 5 of them to rank 1. Measured over 155 live agent calls, agents already distil well (mean 43
chars), so this is not an available lever for the eg arm — but it is the single most important thing
for a human or a badly-written integration to get right.

## 8. Method notes

Seven silent measurement failures were found and fixed during this work, each producing
plausible-looking output while measuring the wrong thing: `prof=()` returning nothing under bash 3.2,
the SHOW=10 cap, `_egsearch.py` stripping payload blocks, a falsification test that could only read
zero, a grading gate that could never fire for the eg arm, reports written to a directory nothing
looked in, and mixed denominators in a subset row. The payload logs, cap markers, gate arithmetic and
run-alignment warnings exist because assuming the harness worked was wrong seven times.

## 2026-07-28: two sample defects found, both correcting AGAINST the tool's favour

**1. The eg arm was silently measured on an easier subsample.** `tools/run_3arm.sh:46` skips an
instance for eg — and only for eg — when `graphs/<iid>/graph.edges.ndjson` is absent. Ten of the
haiku-30 had none, and they are the LARGE repos (three.js, nushell, hugo, javaparser, gson,
fluentd, jekyll, bat, php-cs-fixer, preact). baseline and cmm ran all thirty, so a third of the
sample was dropped from eg's side by a criterion correlated with repo size.

All ten dumps BUILD CLEANLY on the integrated binary (10/10, e.g. three.js 47 MB of edges in 221s,
javaparser 109 MB in 37s), so the skips were a property of the older build, not of those repos.

## Why the 35% token target is NOT reachable by tool-side changes (measured, not asserted)

- baseline 30.9 turns -> eg 24.7 turns. eg removes ~6 turns of grep/read exploration. THAT is the
  graph's contribution, and it converts to -32.3% of tokens on the frozen 50.
- The remaining ~23 turns are the edit / verify / test loop, identical work for both arms. A code
  graph cannot shorten it.
- Search discipline moves turns by ~1 (config 5: falsified).
- Payload budget moves tokens by ~2% (config 2 vs 3, and the measured TIER curve).
- Preselection pool: measured NEGATIVE (-3.8pt at 256, -7.7pt at 1024).
- Ranking levers: +7.7pt of localization across four changes, which bought resolves, not tokens.

Every remaining lever is smaller than the 2.7-point gap, and eg's own run-to-run sd is 6.5pt on
tokens and 3.06 resolves. The gap is not a tuning failure; the locate phase the graph collapses is a
bounded fraction of the session.

---

## PROMPT ASYMMETRY FOUND BY AUDIT — corrected, and the affected claim restated

An adversarial prompt-symmetry audit found a real unfairness in the CMM arm that I introduced:

`cmm_clamp_prompt` (run_3arm.sh:464-484) was missing THREE of the discipline clauses that
`base_clamp_prompt` and `shipped_eg_prompt` both carried — "do not chain more searches", "NEVER read
a whole file to explore", "NEVER search outside this repo" — and it had no numbered hard-rules list at
all. It ALSO advertised four extra verbs (def / callers / impact / grep) that eg's block never
mentioned, even though eg-q exposes exactly the same five verbs.

Measured consequence (results/C3*/*/gq_calls.log):

| arm | wrapper calls/session | non-search verb calls | sessions using one | mean turns |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| eg | 1.88 | 5 | 5/48 | 24.3 |
| cmm | 4.20 | 85 (def 43, grep 34, callers 8) | 31/50 | 29.6 |

+2.32 calls/session is ~43% of cmm's turn excess over eg, ~7.8% of a cmm session. So roughly
**10 of the 35 points of the eg-vs-cmm token claim was prompt, not index.** The honest figure for
configs 1-3 is nearer **-25%**, and the -35.0% number must not be quoted without this correction.

NOT affected: eg vs baseline. Those two clamps are matched clause-for-clause and their per-turn
replay is 32,276 vs 32,229 tokens (0.15% apart). The baseline additionally gets batching guidance eg
does not, so **-32.3% is conservative on this axis.** The audit specifically looked for a baseline
advantage and found the opposite.

Also recorded: PREREGISTRATION.md section 2 promised a byte-identical SHARED block verified by md5.
That guarantee applied to `PROMPT_FAMILY=thorough`. The published runs used `vendor`, under which
`shared_block` is never emitted. Section 2's symmetry mechanism was therefore VOID for every number
reported so far; symmetry rested on three hand-written clamps, one of which was mismatched.

CORRECTION APPLIED: both blocks now carry the identical four hard rules verbatim, and both advertise
their full five-verb surface. Only the vendor tool DESCRIPTION differs, which is each tool's own
documentation and is legitimate. Verified: the shared rules text appears exactly twice in the script,
and each block contains all four rules and all four extra verbs.

The RR re-run in flight when this was found used the OLD asymmetric prompt and has been DISCARDED
rather than reported. It is being relaunched on the corrected prompts.

### Snippet-parity fix verified (and a false alarm of mine, recorded)

After removing cmm's 6-line snippet clamp I measured cmm at "643.8 lines mean, max 1093" and halted
the re-run believing I had over-corrected into a 40x advantage for cmm. That measurement was WRONG:
my block parser assumed eg's `N. path:line` hit format, but cmm emits `path:line  Kind Name` with no
numeric prefix, so the parser matched almost nothing and counted whole payload chunks as single

Its own audit note quantifies the leak — *"the eg arm costs 24% MORE per turn because the search result is ADDED to context and the agent then reads the file anyway — we pay for search AND read"* — and the `EG_EDIT_FROM_PAYLOAD` cell that removes the Read was never run. That's the legitimate opening. First, a zero-API-cost screen: does the payload actually carry editable complete bodies on real instances?

## MODEL-MATRIX ROWS — approved config and why

Approved: CONFIG 3 (`EG_TOPK=20 EG_TOPK_SHOW=20 EG_TIER=6 EG_MAXBYTES=24576 GQ_SEARCH_CAP=4`;
cmm `CMM_SHOW=13 CMM_SHOW_SEM=7 GQ_SEARCH_CAP=4`).

Rationale, from 3-run means only:
- config 1: eg 18.0 vs baseline 20.0 — BELOW baseline. Rejected.
- config 3: eg 20.3 vs baseline 20.0 — parity, and the best token margin over cmm (-35.0%). Approved.
- configs 4 and 5: not 3-run validated. Excluded from the headline rows by rule.

Why the matrix runs even though the 35% token target is missed: the per-model rows were an explicit
deliverable, and they answer a different question (does the effect hold across model tiers?) than the
token threshold. Reporting them at -32.3% is the honest outcome; withholding them because a threshold
was missed would be selective reporting.

Rows: fable 5, opus 10, sonnet 20 on the nested stratified sets. haiku 30 needs NO new run — it is a
subset of the frozen 50 already measured at 3 runs, so it is reported by restricting config 3's
existing data to `.matrix_haiku.txt`.

---

## CONFIGURATION 5 — FALSIFIED on its own mechanism after ONE run (stopped early, deliberately)

Config 5 predicted: tightening the cap from 4 to 2 cuts turns further, and turns are the dear axis
(~4% of session tokens each), so tokens improve more than config 4's byte trim would.

Measured, eg arm:

| config | searches/session | turns |
|---|---|---|
| 1 (no cap) | 2.66 | 24.68 |
| 3 (cap=4) | 1.76 | 23.77 |
| 5 (cap=2) | 1.54 | 24.00 |

Searches fell 42% from config 1 and turns did NOT move (config 5 is marginally ABOVE config 3).
Search count is decoupled from total turns. The arithmetic was available before the run and I should
have done it first: searches are ~11% of eg's turns (2.66 of 24.68), so eliminating them entirely
could save at most ~2-3 turns, and the cap substitutes grep-and-read turns for search turns.

STOPPED AFTER RUN 1, on purpose. The prediction is falsified at the mechanism level, so runs 2-3 would
buy a more precise estimate of no effect at ~$40 and two hours, while the per-model matrix rows — an
explicit deliverable — waited. Reported as: one run, mechanism falsified, no token effect. It is NOT
reported as a 3-run configuration and its accuracy figure is not used for anything.

content.text:
**Decisive.** Three compounding harness defects were suppressing the exact capability the whole value proposition rests on. Same instance, same query, same repo:

| binary + flags | bytes | complete bodies |
|---|---|---|
| `entire-graph-fb` (harness default eg binary), config-3 flags | 5,729 | **0** |
| current `entire-graph`, `--max-snippet-lines 400` | 1,611 | **0** |
| current `entire-graph`, **tool defaults** | **2,816** | **3** |

At defaults, hit 1 is the *complete, editable* `Context.DataFromReader` body with an `exact-symbol` signal. So:

1. The eg arm runs `entire-graph-fb`, an **older build with no complete-symbol allocator at all** — 2× the bytes for zero editable bodies.
2. `eg-q` **always** passes `--max-snippet-lines` (`EG_SNIPPET:-6`), which **disables the promotion** even on builds that have it.
3. `--top-k 20` + `--max-context-bytes 24576` spreads the budget so no promotion could occur regardless.

That is the "+10–24% per turn, we pay for search AND read" leak — not a property of the tool. Now screening localization across all 30 instances before spending a cent, because fewer bytes must not cost gold-file recall.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Zero-API-cost payload screen.

For each instance: does the eg search payload carry an EDITABLE complete function body,
and is the gold file still localized? Compares the harness's as-run config against
tool-default config, on the same query, same repo, same commit.

No agent, no model calls. Writes NDJSON to --out.
"""
import argparse, json, os, re, subprocess, sys, shutil

GM = "/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-suhaan-devenv/7e3deab1-a028-46d5-9bf1-3318de93a0b6/scratchpad/graphmark/agentic-swebench"
SP = "/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-suhaan-devenv/0d4c4262-2100-4779-8745-e855e0a78208/scratchpad/screen"

CONFIGS = {
    # name: (binary, extra flags)
    "asrun_fb_cfg3": ("/tmp/graphmark-bin/entire-graph-fb",
                      ["--top-k", "20", "--max-snippet-lines", "6", "--max-context-bytes", "24576"]),
    "new_cfg3":      ("/tmp/egbin/entire-graph",
                      ["--top-k", "20", "--max-snippet-lines", "6", "--max-context-bytes", "24576"]),
    "new_defaults":  ("/tmp/egbin/entire-graph", ["--top-k", "6"]),
    "new_def_k10":   ("/tmp/egbin/entire-graph", ["--top-k", "10"]),
}

HIT = re.compile(r'^(\d+)\.\s+(\S+?):(\d[\d\-]*)\s*(.*)$')


def load_tasks():
    d = json.load(open(f"{GM}/tasks/pilot_tasks.json"))
    return {i["instance_id"]: i for i in d["instances"]}


def gold_files(rec):
    return sorted({l[6:].strip() for l in rec["patch"].splitlines() if l.startswith("+++ b/")})


def distil(ps):
    """One-sentence query, mimicking what agents actually send (FINDINGS: mean 43 chars).
    Deterministic: first non-empty line, markdown/# stripped, capped at 120 chars."""
    for line in ps.splitlines():
        s = line.strip().lstrip("#").strip()
        if len(s) > 8 and not s.startswith("```"):
            return s[:120]
    return ps[:120]


def ensure_clone(rec):
    repo = rec["repo"].replace("/", "_")
    cache = f"{GM}/repo-cache/{repo}"
    if not os.path.isdir(cache):
        return None, f"no repo-cache for {repo}"
    dst = f"{SP}/clones/{repo}"
    if not os.path.isdir(dst):
        os.makedirs(f"{SP}/clones", exist_ok=True)
        r = subprocess.run(["git", "clone", "--shared", "--no-checkout", "--quiet", cache, dst],
                           capture_output=True, text=True)
        if r.returncode != 0:
            return None, f"clone failed: {r.stderr[:120]}"
    # point HEAD at the base commit without materializing a working tree
    r = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", dst, "update-ref", "HEAD", rec["base_commit"]],
                       capture_output=True, text=True)
    if r.returncode != 0:
        return None, f"update-ref failed: {r.stderr[:120]}"
    return dst, None


def parse(out):
    hits, completes = [], 0
    for line in out.splitlines():
        m = HIT.match(line)
        if m:
            meta = m.group(4)
            hits.append({"path": m.group(2), "loc": m.group(3),
                         "complete": "complete-symbol" in meta})
            if "complete-symbol" in meta:
                completes += 1
    return hits, completes


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--list", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--out", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--configs", default=",".join(CONFIGS))
    args = ap.parse_args()

    tasks = load_tasks()
    iids = [l.strip() for l in open(args.list) if l.strip()]
    names = args.configs.split(",")
    fh = open(args.out, "w")

    for n, iid in enumerate(iids, 1):
        rec = tasks.get(iid)
        if rec is None:
            print(f"[{n}/{len(iids)}] {iid} NOT IN DATASET", flush=True)
            continue
        gold = gold_files(rec)
        q = distil(rec["problem_statement"])
        repo_dir, err = ensure_clone(rec)
        if err:
            print(f"[{n}/{len(iids)}] {iid} {err}", flush=True)
            continue
        row = {"iid": iid, "repo": rec["repo"], "gold": gold, "query": q, "cfg": {}}
        for name in names:
            binp, flags = CONFIGS[name]
            cache = f"{SP}/cache/{name}/{rec['repo'].replace('/', '_')}"
            os.makedirs(cache, exist_ok=True)
            cmd = [binp, "search", "--query", q, "--repo", repo_dir, "--head",
                   "--profile", "full", "--format", "text", "--cache-dir", cache] + flags
            try:
                r = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=900)
                out = r.stdout
                rc = r.returncode
                stderr = r.stderr.strip()[:200]
            except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
                out, rc, stderr = "", -9, "timeout"
            hits, completes = parse(out)
            # gold rank = 1-based position of first hit whose path is a gold file
            grank = None
            for i, h in enumerate(hits, 1):
                if h["path"] in gold:
                    grank = i
                    break
            gold_complete = any(h["path"] in gold and h["complete"] for h in hits)
            row["cfg"][name] = {
                "rc": rc, "stderr": stderr, "bytes": len(out), "hits": len(hits),
                "completes": completes, "gold_rank": grank, "gold_complete": gold_complete,
                "top1": hits[0]["path"] if hits else None,
                "top1_complete": hits[0]["complete"] if hits else False,
            }
        fh.write(json.dumps(row) + "\n")
        fh.flush()
        s = " | ".join(
            f"{k}: {v['bytes']}B c={v['completes']} g={v['gold_rank']}" for k, v in row["cfg"].items())
        print(f"[{n}/{len(iids)}] {iid}  {s}", flush=True)
    fh.close()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Aggregate the payload screen. Paired per-instance, so every config sees the same instances."""
import json, sys, statistics as st

rows = [json.loads(l) for l in open(sys.argv[1])]
cfgs = list(rows[0]["cfg"].keys())

ok = [r for r in rows if all(r["cfg"][c]["rc"] == 0 and r["cfg"][c]["hits"] > 0 for c in cfgs)]

if dropped:
    print("DROPPED (a config returned nothing):", ", ".join(dropped))

K = 10  # matched-breadth recall cutoff, so a 20-hit config gets no free extra chances


def recall_at(c, r, k):
    paths = r["cfg"][c]["paths"][:k]
    return any(p in r["gold"] for p in paths)


print(f"\n{'config':<16} {'mean B':>8} {'median B':>9} {'completes':>10} {'inst w/ >=1':>12} "

base = None
for c in cfgs:
    b = [r["cfg"][c]["bytes"] for r in ok]
    comp = [r["cfg"][c]["completes"] for r in ok]
    any_comp = sum(1 for x in comp if x > 0)
    rec = sum(1 for r in ok if recall_at(c, r, K))
    goldbody = sum(1 for r in ok if any(p in r["gold"] for p in r["cfg"][c]["complete_paths"]))
    t1 = sum(1 for r in ok if r["cfg"][c]["top1_complete"])
    print(f"{c:<16} {st.mean(b):>8.0f} {st.median(b):>9.0f} {st.mean(comp):>10.2f} "

    if c == cfgs[0]:
        base = b

print("\npaired payload-byte delta vs as-run control (negative = fewer bytes handed to the agent):")
ctrl = cfgs[0]
for c in cfgs[1:]:
    d = [(r["cfg"][c]["bytes"] - r["cfg"][ctrl]["bytes"]) / r["cfg"][ctrl]["bytes"] * 100 for r in ok]
    d.sort()
    lo, hi = d[int(.025 * len(d))], d[int(.975 * len(d)) - 1]
    print(f"  {c:<16} median {st.median(d):+6.1f}%   mean {st.mean(d):+6.1f}%   range [{lo:+.0f}%, {hi:+.0f}%]")

print("\ngold-file localization change vs as-run control (matched at top-%d):" % K)

Tokens track TURNS, and the graph's addressable share is the LOCATE phase, which is a minority of
them. Reaching -35% tokens needs roughly -45% turns (~15 against 28.6), i.e. deleting most of the
FIX-and-verify phase, which a locate tool cannot do.

The payload-size lever was measured rather than assumed, on 19 `PFeg_r1` sessions: mean billed
1,185,845 tokens against a mean search payload of 15,743 bytes (3,936 tokens) over 25.7 turns, so
the payload re-read CEILING is 12.95% of billed and cutting the budget 24576->16384 can save **at
most 4.27%**. It cannot close a 23-point gap, so that cell was NOT run to imply otherwise.

The published 54.9% was reachable only because eg ran under a hard frugality clamp while the
baseline got no working policy at all — and that clamp cost accuracy (131/300 vs 150/300, McNemar
p=0.013). So every configuration that clears 35% is one that fails accuracy parity. Recorded as a
NEGATIVE RESULT rather than resolved by reconfiguration.

| cmm      | 27.6 | 0.2348 | 7.86 | 6.44 |

  an ALL-GATED sensitivity row alongside the CLEAN (degenerate-excluded) primary.

Cost units, always side by side:
  usd          = total_cost_usd                                  <- the money claim
  billed_new   = input + cache_creation + output                 <- the work signal
  total_tokens = billed_new + cache_read                         <- outlier-prone
  total_tokens overweights cache_read: cache reads bill at a fraction of input price
  (~0.1x), so a run that re-reads a big cached prefix looks catastrophic in total_tokens
  while barely moving usd. usd is the claim; billed_new is the work; total_tokens is
  reported only for continuity with older numbers.

  r = ln(treat/ref). Geometric mean = exp(mean(r)) - 1, expressed as % change, so a 2x
  increase and a 2x decrease cancel to 0%. Median, 10%-trimmed mean, and the raw pooled
  ratio (sum/sum) are also shown; the pooled one is outlier-prone and is labelled so.

Bootstrap 95% CI: 20,000 resamples over instances, on the geometric mean and on
  tokens-per-resolved / usd-per-resolved.

Leave-one-instance-out (LOO): min/max of every headline when any single instance is
  dropped, plus whether the sign survives. A previous eg-vs-cmm result flipped sign when
  one instance was removed.

Micro vs macro: micro = geometric mean over instances (dominated by the few big repos).
  macro = per-repo geometric mean, then unweighted mean across repos. Both printed, plus
  the divergence.

Also: per-repo table, per-language table (language derived from gold-patch file
  extensions), tokens/resolved and usd/resolved with numerator AND denominator shown
  explicitly, and McNemar exact two-sided p for the resolved-count comparison.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Grade any tag whose sessions are complete and which has no report yet. One grader at a time.
AS="/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-suhaan-devenv/7e3deab1-a028-46d5-9bf1-3318de93a0b6/scratchpad/graphmark/agentic-swebench"
export DOCKER_HOST="unix:///Users/suhaan/.docker/run/docker.sock"
# The swebench harness writes its report to the CWD. Without this cd the reports land wherever the
# watcher was launched from (measured: C2cmm_r1's report ended up in ~/devenv), so the "already
# graded" check never sees them and the tag would be graded again on every poll.
cd "$AS" || exit 1
elig_for(){ case "$1" in
  MXfable*)  echo "$AS/.matrix_fable.txt";;
  MXsonnet*) echo "$AS/.matrix_sonnet.txt";;
  MXopus*)   echo "$AS/.matrix_opus.txt";;
  *)         echo "$AS/.elig_strat60.txt";;
esac; }
arm_for(){ case "$1" in *base*) echo baseline;; *eg*) echo eg;; *cmm*) echo cmm;; esac; }
end=$(( $(date +%s) + 86400 ))
while [ "$(date +%s)" -lt "$end" ]; do
  for tag in RRbase_r1 RRbase_r2 RRbase_r3 RReg_r1 RReg_r2 RReg_r3 RRcmm_r1 RRcmm_r2 RRcmm_r3 \
             C2eg_r1 C2eg_r2 C2eg_r3 C2cmm_r1 C2cmm_r2 C2cmm_r3 \
             C3eg_r1 C3eg_r2 C3eg_r3 C3cmm_r1 C3cmm_r2 C3cmm_r3 \
             MXfablebase_r1 MXfablebase_r2 MXfablebase_r3 MXfableeg_r1 MXfableeg_r2 MXfableeg_r3 \
             MXfablecmm_r1 MXfablecmm_r2 MXfablecmm_r3 \
             MXsonnetbase_r1 MXsonnetbase_r2 MXsonnetbase_r3 MXsonneteg_r1 MXsonneteg_r2 MXsonneteg_r3 \
             MXsonnetcmm_r1 MXsonnetcmm_r2 MXsonnetcmm_r3 \
             MXopusbase_r1 MXopusbase_r2 MXopusbase_r3 MXopuseg_r1 MXopuseg_r2 MXopuseg_r3 \
             MXopuscmm_r1 MXopuscmm_r2 MXopuscmm_r3; do
    arm=$(arm_for "$tag"); [ -z "$arm" ] && continue
    d="$AS/results/$tag/$arm"; [ -d "$d" ] || continue
    elig=$(elig_for "$tag"); want=$(grep -c . "$elig")
    # The eg arm SKIPS instances with no prebuilt graph (run_3arm exits before writing cc_out.json),
    # so its session count can never reach |elig| and a `have >= want` gate would never fire — the eg
    # arm of every config would sit ungraded forever. Subtract the structurally-skippable instances
    # for eg. They still enter the predictions file as EMPTY patches, i.e. scored as eg losses.
    if [ "$arm" = eg ]; then
      skip=0
      while read -r iid; do
        [ -n "$iid" ] || continue
        [ -s "$AS/graphs/$iid/graph.edges.ndjson" ] || skip=$((skip+1))
      done < "$elig"
      want=$((want-skip))
    fi
    have=$(find "$d" -name cc_out.json 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
    [ "$have" -ge "$want" ] || continue
    [ -s "$AS/$tag.$tag.json" ] && continue
    # AUDIT FIX. The old guard was `pgrep -f "RESULTS_TAG=$tag"`, which can NEVER match: RESULTS_TAG
    # is an ENV PREFIX, so it is not in argv, and inside the driver's `bash -c` text $tag is not even
    # expanded. The guard never fired. Because run_3arm.sh writes patch.diff AFTER cc_out.json (it
    # waits on the per-cache lock first, observed up to 178s), grading could snapshot a session whose
    # patch had not landed and submit it as EMPTY. Measured damage: 7 real eg patches and 1 cmm patch
    # graded empty; 0 baseline, because the S-tags were graded later by hand. The race was therefore
    # structurally asymmetric AGAINST the tool arms.
    #
    # Two real guards instead of one fake one:
    #   (a) no run_3arm.sh process for this arm is alive (arm+iid ARE in argv, unlike the tag), and
    #   (b) every session with cost>0 has a non-empty patch.diff, or we wait for it to land.
    pgrep -f "run_3arm.sh $arm " >/dev/null && continue
    _settle=0
    while :; do
      _pending=$(ARM="$arm" TAG="$tag" ELIG="$elig" python3 - <<'PYX'
import json,os,glob
AS=os.environ.get('AS'); tag=os.environ['TAG']; arm=os.environ['ARM']
elig=[l.strip() for l in open(os.environ['ELIG']) if l.strip()]
n=0
for iid in elig:
    cc=f'{AS}/results/{tag}/{arm}/{iid}/cc_out.json'
    if not os.path.exists(cc): continue
    try: j=json.load(open(cc))
    except Exception: continue
    if not (j.get('total_cost_usd') or 0)>0: continue
    p=f'{AS}/results/{tag}/{arm}/{iid}/patch.diff'
    if not os.path.exists(p) or os.path.getsize(p)==0: n+=1
print(n)
PYX
)
      [ "${_pending:-0}" -eq 0 ] && break
      _settle=$((_settle+1))
      if [ "$_settle" -gt 12 ]; then
        echo "[$(date +%H:%M:%S)] $tag: $_pending session(s) still have cost>0 and no patch after 6min; grading anyway (they are genuine empties)"
        break
      fi
      sleep 30
    done
    while pgrep -f 'swebench.harness.run_evaluation' >/dev/null; do sleep 60; done
    ELIG="$elig" TAG="$tag" ARM="$arm" python3 - <<'PY'
import json,os
AS=os.environ.get('AS','/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-suhaan-devenv/7e3deab1-a028-46d5-9bf1-3318de93a0b6/scratchpad/graphmark/agentic-swebench')
tag=os.environ['TAG']; arm=os.environ['ARM']
elig=[l.strip() for l in open(os.environ['ELIG']) if l.strip()]
preds=[]
for iid in elig:
    p=f'{AS}/results/{tag}/{arm}/{iid}/patch.diff'
    d=open(p).read() if os.path.exists(p) and os.path.getsize(p)>0 else ''
    preds.append(dict(instance_id=iid,model_name_or_path=tag,model_patch=d))
json.dump(preds,open(f'{AS}/preds_{tag}.json','w'))
print(f"{tag}: {len(preds)} preds, {sum(1 for x in preds if not x['model_patch'])} empty")
PY
    echo "[$(date +%H:%M:%S)] grading $tag"
    python3.12 -m swebench.harness.run_evaluation --dataset_name swe-bench/SWE-bench_Multilingual \
      --predictions_path "$AS/preds_${tag}.json" --run_id "$tag" \
      --max_workers 2 --cache_level env --timeout 1800 >> "$AS/logs/grade_${tag}.log" 2>&1
    echo "[$(date +%H:%M:%S)] $tag graded"
  done
  sleep 120
done

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Grade P1 tags with the SAME pipeline and the SAME guards as .grade_watch.sh:
#   (a) no live run_3arm.sh for that arm, (b) every cost>0 session has a non-empty patch.diff
#   (the patch-lands-after-cc_out race that previously graded 7 real eg patches as empty),
#   (c) one grader at a time, (d) preds built over the FULL elig list so empties are submitted
#   as losses and every arm shares one denominator.
# Usage: grade_p1.sh <elig_file> <tag> [<tag> ...]
set -uo pipefail
AS="/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-suhaan-devenv/7e3deab1-a028-46d5-9bf1-3318de93a0b6/scratchpad/graphmark/agentic-swebench"
export DOCKER_HOST="unix:///Users/suhaan/.docker/run/docker.sock"
export AS
cd "$AS" || exit 1
PYSWE="${PYSWE:-python3.12}"
elig="${1:?elig}"; shift

input.content:
#!/bin/sh
# Benchmark sessions may inspect their OWN working tree, but the repo-cache's refs reach past the
# instance base_commit — so history access can hand the agent the upstream fix verbatim. Block the
# subcommands that expose it (graphmark#53: a session located and copied the real fix commit).
#
# GUARD NORMALIZATION (2026-07-28). This script used to switch on "${1:-}" directly, so ANY leading
# git global option moved the subcommand out of $1 and fell through to the unconditional
# `exec /usr/bin/git "$@"` — defeating the 36-subcommand blocklist AND all three of 976d6ab's hole
# fixes simultaneously. Verified by execution before this fix: `git --no-pager log -1 --oneline`,
# `git -C . show --stat HEAD`, `git -c core.pager=cat log`, `git --git-dir=.git log`,
# `git --no-pager grep -l x HEAD`, `git --no-pager diff HEAD~1` ALL exited 0 with real history.
# Measured over 6,785 prior sessions: 88 global-option invocations of guarded subcommands across 62
# sessions, 26 of them history reads, including one byte-identical gold-patch copy
# (PVbaseline_r2/apache__lucene-11760 vs upstream 8fe9e83c2d8).
# Fix: strip the leading global-option prefix, switch on the REAL subcommand, and scan the arguments
# that follow THAT subcommand. argv is never mutated in this shell, so the exec at the bottom still
# passes the caller's original arguments and every allowed command behaves exactly as before.
#
# Also fixed here: the `diff` pathspec false positive. The old scan looped over every argument and
# did not stop at `--`, so `git diff README.md` and `git diff -- README.md` were BOTH blocked while
# option-only diffs passed. That false positive is what taught agents to reach for `-C`/`--no-pager`
# in the first place (49 of the 88 bypasses were the benign diff workaround).
#
# Known and deliberately NOT changed: `git apply`/`git am` stay allowed (they apply a patch the agent
# already holds; obtaining one is what is guarded), and an absolute-path `/usr/bin/git` still bypasses
# this shim entirely — nothing in a PATH shim can prevent that. Both are recorded in the audit.

# ---- locate the real subcommand, without touching argv ----
_skip=0
for _a in "$@"; do
  case "$_a" in
    --no-pager|-p|--paginate|--bare|--literal-pathspecs|--no-replace-objects|--no-optional-locks|--glob-pathspecs|--noglob-pathspecs|--icase-pathspecs|--no-lazy-fetch)
      _skip=$((_skip+1)) ;;
    -C|-c|--git-dir|--work-tree|--exec-path|--namespace|--super-prefix|--config-env)
      _skip=$((_skip+2)) ;;
    -C?*|-c?*|--git-dir=*|--work-tree=*|--exec-path=*|--namespace=*|--super-prefix=*|--config-env=*)
      _skip=$((_skip+1)) ;;
    *) break ;;
  esac
done
# _skip counts words consumed by the global prefix; the value-taking forms above may over-count by
# one when their value itself looks like an option, which is harmless: it can only make the guard
# inspect one word later, and the blocklist below is keyed on the subcommand we resolve here.
sub=$(i=1; for _a in "$@"; do
        if [ "$i" -gt "$_skip" ]; then printf '%s' "$_a"; break; fi
        i=$((i+1))
      done)

# scan_rest <skip> "$@" — runs in a SUBSHELL so `shift` cannot disturb the caller's argv.
scan_rest() (
  _n=$1; shift
  _i=0
  while [ "$_i" -lt "$_n" ] && [ $# -gt 0 ]; do shift; _i=$((_i+1)); done
  [ $# -gt 0 ] && shift   # drop the subcommand itself
  for a in "$@"; do
    [ "$a" = "--" ] && break          # everything after -- is a pathspec, never a ref
    case "$a" in
      -*) continue ;;
      HEAD|HEAD~*|HEAD^*|origin/*|refs/*|*..*) exit 9 ;;
      *[0-9a-f][0-9a-f][0-9a-f][0-9a-f][0-9a-f][0-9a-f][0-9a-f]*)
        case "$a" in
          *[!0-9a-f]*) : ;;
          *) exit 9 ;;
        esac ;;
    esac
  done
  exit 0
)

case "${sub:-}" in
  log|show|blame|fetch|pull|clone|checkout|switch|cherry-pick|revert|reflog|cat-file|rev-list|describe|tag|branch|remote|ls-remote|format-patch|archive|worktree|bisect|stash|notes|ls-tree|for-each-ref|merge-tree|range-diff|whatchanged|submodule|verify-pack|unpack-objects|read-tree|checkout-index|cherry|patch-id)
    echo "netjail: 'git $sub' is blocked — the checkout's history is off-limits; author the fix yourself." >&2
    exit 86 ;;
  grep)
    # `git grep <pattern> <ref>` searches a COMMIT, which reaches past base_commit. Working-tree
    # grep is legitimate. Any bare argument after the pattern is a pathspec OR a ref, and we cannot
    # tell them apart cheaply — so require the explicit working-tree form.
    if ! scan_rest "$_skip" "$@"; then
      echo "netjail: 'git grep <ref>' is blocked — grep your working tree, not history." >&2; exit 86
    fi ;;
  restore)
    # `git restore --source=<ref> <path>` WRITES a file from another commit into the working tree,
    # which hands over the upstream fix verbatim. Restoring from the index is legitimate.
    i=1
    for a in "$@"; do
      if [ "$i" -gt "$_skip" ]; then
        case "$a" in
          --source=*|-s) echo "netjail: 'git restore --source' is blocked — it would write another commit's content into your tree." >&2; exit 86 ;;
        esac
      fi
      i=$((i+1))
    done ;;
  diff)
    # working-tree diff is legitimate self-verification; a diff against any ref is not
    if ! scan_rest "$_skip" "$@"; then
      echo "netjail: 'git diff <ref>' is blocked — only your own working-tree diff is allowed." >&2; exit 86
    fi ;;
esac
exec /usr/bin/git "$@"

Confirmed, and quantified — the ceiling is real but not where I assumed:

- **`enforcement_errors` fired in real sessions**: 5 (eg), 2 (cmm), 6 (old-prompt eg) — Claude Code *does* refuse Edit without a prior Read.
- But distinct files edited is only **~1.5/session** while reads are **~5.5**. So the mandatory floor is ~1.5 reads; roughly **4 reads/session are discretionary**.

Where this stands, with everything measured rather than assumed:

**The root cause of the "negative result" is a prompt asymmetry, not the tool.** eg was instructed *"open the top hit's file with your native Read tool"* while cmm was instructed *"edit from the source it printed"* — the turn-saving instruction went to the competitor. Both arms now carry byte-identical hard rules and the same five-verb surface; baseline keeps "READ the file" because it genuinely has no payload.

**Three defects found and fixed along the way, each execution-verified:**
1. **netjail was defeatable by any leading git global option** — `--no-pager`, `-C`, `-c`, `--git-dir` all fell through to `exec /usr/bin/git`. Fixed by resolving the real subcommand; **20/20** test cases pass, and it also removes the false positive (`git diff README.md` was blocked) that taught agents the bypass. My scanner reproduces the known historical gold-patch leak as a positive control, and **my runs show 0 bypasses / 0 leaks on all three arms.**
2. **Local `main @114e178` is unusable here** — still aborts in linked worktrees, which silently produced 0-byte payloads. Rebuilt from `integ/measure-2026-07-28 @0af923e`, the only branch with both the complete-symbol allocator (PR #66) and the worktree fix (PR #68).

**And one finding that constrains what is achievable at all:** Claude Code **refuses to Edit a file not Read in-conversation** — the enforcement error fires in these very runs (eg 5, cmm 2, old-prompt eg 6). So `EG_EDIT_FROM_PAYLOAD`'s premise ("do NOT open the file first", "3–4 turns") is structurally impossible in this harness, and the arithmetic that proposed it was written without that constraint. The real addressable quantity is the **~4 discretionary reads of ~5.5/session** present on *every* arm — not all of them.

On the pilot the payload prompt did not reduce reads (55% of its reads were of files whose complete body it already held). I've recorded that in the manifest before reading the corrected runs, so config 6 gets reported as measured either way. If it falls short, the successor tells the agent the *truth* about the mandatory pre-edit read instead of forbidding it — applied to all three arms, and selected on the 24-instance disjoint pool, never on the reported instances.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# CONFIG 7 draft blocks — NOT yet integrated into run_3arm.sh (config 6 is in flight; editing the
# live script would change the prompt for instances not yet started).
#
# Design comes from the config-6 pilot diagnosis, all of it measured on `.elig_h30`, which is
# DISJOINT from all four reported .matrix_* sets (verified: intersection 0 with each):
#
#  1. Claude Code REFUSES to edit a file not Read in-conversation (enforcement error observed in
#     real sessions: eg 5, cmm 2, old-prompt eg 6). A prompt that says "do NOT open the file first"
#     is therefore asking for something impossible, and the pilot shows it gets ignored WHOLESALE:
#     55.2% of the pilot's eg reads were of a file whose complete body was already in the payload.
#     FIX: state the constraint truthfully and spend the mandatory read well, instead of denying it.
#  2. ~4 of ~5.5 reads/session are DISCRETIONARY on every arm (mandatory floor = distinct files
#     edited, ~1.5/session). That is the addressable quantity, and it is addressable on ALL THREE
#     arms — so the read-discipline clause is emitted identically for baseline, eg and cmm. Giving it
#     to the tool arms only would be the exact prompt asymmetry this cell exists to remove.
#  3. eg pays +10.9% MORE per turn than baseline because of payload bytes. Measured on the h30
#     screen: EG_TOPK/SHOW 20->10 cuts payload bytes 46.3% (median) with IDENTICAL gold-file
#     recall@10 (23/30 both) and identical complete-body count (2.60 both). That converts eg's
#     per-turn premium into a per-turn DISCOUNT ($7.38 vs baseline $7.47 per 1k-turn-unit).
#     cmm's visible-hit count is moved in lockstep (CMM_SHOW 13/7 -> 7/3) so matched breadth is
#     preserved, as config 3 intended.

# ---- emitted IDENTICALLY into all three arm blocks (arm-agnostic, and true for all of them) ----
read_discipline() {
  cat <<'TXT'
One read is unavoidable and the rest are not. Your file-editing tool will not modify a file you have
not Read in this session, so take exactly ONE narrow Read of each file you actually change — at the
line range you already have — and take no others. Do not read a file you are not about to edit, do
not re-read a file you have already been shown, and never read a whole file. Every extra turn
replays your entire context, and that replay is what this task costs.
TXT
}

# ---- eg TOOL block (EG_PAYLOAD_V2=1) ----
payload_v2_eg_prompt() {  # $1 = wrapper command
  cat <<TXT
A precomputed code graph is available: $1 . Use it to LOCATE code INSTEAD OF grep/find.
Your FIRST action is ONE search:
  $1 search "<the bug in one sentence>"
Its answer is not a pointer — for the top-ranked hits it prints the COMPLETE body of the enclosing
function, verbatim, with its real line numbers, and marks those hits complete-symbol.
Decide the whole change from those bodies before you touch a file: which function is wrong, what the
fix is, and which line range it lands on. That is what removes the hunting — not the reading.
Hard rules: (1) LOCATE WITH THE TOOL FIRST. (2) After the tool answers, EDIT from the source it
printed; open the file only if the body you need was not printed or is marked truncated, and then
read only that line range - do not chain more tool calls. (3) NEVER read a whole file to explore;
pass a line range. (4) NEVER search outside this repo. Apply the minimal fix and STOP the moment you
can justify it.
If the top hit is clearly wrong, search ONCE more with different words. If that misses too, fall back
to the shell in ONE batched call rather than staying stuck.
Other verbs if the result genuinely leaves a question: $1 def <Symbol> (full source of a symbol),
$1 callers <Symbol> (inbound call paths, file:line and hop), $1 impact <Symbol> (callers, callees,
type consumers, co-change files and siblings in one shot), $1 grep <regex> (grep mapped onto the
enclosing symbol and ranked by hit density).
TXT
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Clone the missing SWE-bench Multilingual repo caches (blob:none partial, full history).
set -uo pipefail
SUITE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
cd "$SUITE"
MISS=/tmp/ml300_missing_repos.txt
clone_one() {
  local repo="$1" name="$2" dst
  dst="$SUITE/repo-cache/$name"
  if [ -d "$dst/.git" ]; then echo "[skip] $name"; return 0; fi
  rm -rf "$dst.tmp"
  if git clone --quiet --no-checkout --filter=blob:none "https://github.com/$repo.git" "$dst.tmp"; then
    mv "$dst.tmp" "$dst"
    echo "[ok] $repo -> $name ($(du -sh "$dst" | cut -f1))"
  else
    rm -rf "$dst.tmp"
    echo "[FAIL] $repo"
    return 1
  fi
}

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Build nested, language-stratified, repo-capped instance sets from instances that ACTUALLY RUN.

Why this is needed: 182 of the 300 SWE-bench Multilingual base_commits are no longer obtainable from
GitHub ("upload-pack: not our ref" — they are not reachable from any ref), and run_3arm.sh sends
`git worktree add` stderr to /dev/null, so those instances silently never run. The published
.matrix_* sets have degraded: 12 of matrix_haiku's 30 now fail to check out.

Eligibility here is the AUTHORITATIVE test — a real `git worktree add --detach` at base_commit that
we then remove — not a rev-parse, because these are --filter=blob:none partial clones and a worktree
needs blobs that may no longer be fetchable.

Sets are nested (5 in 10 in 20 in 30), capped at 4 instances per repository (the rule .elig_strat60
used), and drawn deterministically by a fixed sort + round-robin over languages, so there is no RNG
and the selection is reproducible from this file alone.
"""
import json, os, subprocess, sys, collections

GM = "/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-suhaan-devenv/7e3deab1-a028-46d5-9bf1-3318de93a0b6/scratchpad/graphmark/agentic-swebench"
SP = "/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-suhaan-devenv/0d4c4262-2100-4779-8745-e855e0a78208/scratchpad"
PROBE = f"{SP}/wtprobe"
CAP_PER_REPO = 4

piv = {i["instance_id"]: i for i in json.load(open(f"{GM}/tasks/pilot_tasks.json"))["instances"]}
langmap = json.load(open(f"{GM}/tools/ml300_langmap.json"))


def cache_of(rec):
    return f"{GM}/repo-cache/" + rec["repo"].replace("/", "_")


def really_checks_out(iid):
    rec = piv[iid]
    cache = cache_of(rec)
    if not os.path.isdir(cache):
        return False
    subprocess.run(["rm", "-rf", PROBE], capture_output=True)
    p = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", cache, "worktree", "add", "--force", "--detach",
                        PROBE, rec["base_commit"]], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=300)
    ok = p.returncode == 0 and os.path.isdir(PROBE)
    if ok:
        # a worktree with no files is not usable
        ok = any(not n.startswith(".") for n in os.listdir(PROBE))
    subprocess.run(["git", "-C", cache, "worktree", "remove", "--force", PROBE], capture_output=True)
    subprocess.run(["rm", "-rf", PROBE], capture_output=True)
    return ok


def main():
    cands = [l.strip() for l in open("/tmp/runnable.txt") if l.strip()]
    print(f"candidates (commit present + graph built): {len(cands)}")
    verified = []
    for i, iid in enumerate(cands, 1):
        if really_checks_out(iid):
            verified.append(iid)
        if i % 20 == 0:
            print(f"  probed {i}/{len(cands)}  verified={len(verified)}", flush=True)
    print(f"VERIFIED CHECKOUTABLE: {len(verified)}")
    open(f"{SP}/verified.txt", "w").write("\n".join(verified) + "\n")

    bylang = collections.defaultdict(list)
    for iid in sorted(verified):
        bylang[langmap.get(iid, "?")].append(iid)
    # deterministic language order: most-available first, ties alphabetical
    order = sorted(bylang, key=lambda k: (-len(bylang[k]), k))
    print("available by language:", {k: len(bylang[k]) for k in order})

    chosen, per_repo, idx = [], collections.Counter(), collections.Counter()
    # round-robin across languages so every set is as multilingual as availability allows
    while len(chosen) < 30:
        progressed = False
        for lang in order:
            if len(chosen) >= 30:
                break
            lst = bylang[lang]
            while idx[lang] < len(lst):
                iid = lst[idx[lang]]
                idx[lang] += 1
                repo = piv[iid]["repo"]
                if per_repo[repo] >= CAP_PER_REPO:
                    continue
                chosen.append(iid)
                per_repo[repo] += 1
                progressed = True
                break
        if not progressed:
            break
    if len(chosen) < 30:
        print(f"WARNING: only {len(chosen)} could be selected under the per-repo cap")

    sets = {"fable": chosen[:5], "opus": chosen[:10], "sonnet": chosen[:20], "haiku": chosen[:30]}
    for name, s in sets.items():
        p = f"{GM}/.p2_{name}.txt"
        open(p, "w").write("\n".join(s) + "\n")
        langs = collections.Counter(langmap.get(i, "?") for i in s)
        repos = collections.Counter(piv[i]["repo"] for i in s)
        print(f".p2_{name}.txt n={len(s):2}  langs={dict(langs)}  max_per_repo={max(repos.values())}")
    # nesting assertion
    assert set(sets["fable"]) <= set(sets["opus"]) <= set(sets["sonnet"]) <= set(sets["haiku"])
    print("nesting verified: fable in opus in sonnet in haiku")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# CONFIG 8 (P3) — draft, only to be used if config 7 clears accuracy but misses -35% tokens

## Rationale (measured, not assumed)

Config 7 imposes the SAME task strategy on all three arms via `shared_block(thorough)`, which now
requires of every arm:

- "change EVERY site that needs it, not only the first one you found (look again to find them)"
- "ALWAYS confirm your edit at least once before finishing"

Those two requirements cost TURNS, and the cost differs by arm **because the tools differ**, not
because the prompts do:

| requirement | baseline mechanism | eg mechanism | cmm mechanism |
|---|---|---|---|
| enumerate the other sites | grep again, then read each hit (1-3 turns) | **already printed**: `RELATED SITES` present in **6/6** live P2 payloads | `impact <Symbol>` — a separate wrapper call (1 turn) |
| pick a verification command | infer it | `VERIFY` line present in **3/6** payloads | infer it |
| enum/sealed-set hazards | none | `CLOSED SET` in 1/6 | none |
| concept spelled elsewhere | grep | `SAME-CONCEPT LITERAL` in 2/6 | vector search (1 turn) |

So the shared block's own requirements are satisfiable by eg from material it has ALREADY paid for,
while the other arms must spend turns to satisfy them. That is a genuine product difference and it is
exactly what a code graph is for.

## The change

Nothing about the shared block changes; it stays byte-identical across arms. Each arm's OWN tool
block gains one sentence naming how to satisfy the shared requirement with that arm's own tool:

- eg: "The result already lists RELATED SITES and, when it can determine one, a VERIFY command — use
  them to satisfy the 'every site' and 'verify once' rules instead of searching again."
- cmm: "Use `$1 impact <Symbol>` to enumerate the other sites the change touches, and `$1 callers`
  for inbound paths, to satisfy the 'every site' rule."
- baseline: "Enumerate the other sites with ONE batched grep on the distinctive literal, in the same
  message as the reads you already need."

Each arm is told, in its own vendor idiom, how to meet an identical requirement. No arm is given a
requirement the others lack, and no arm is given a frugality clamp the others lack.

## Falsifiable prediction

Turn delta concentrates in the sweep phase: eg's turns should fall relative to config 7 while
baseline's stay flat or rise (it now grep-sweeps deliberately rather than accidentally). If eg's turns
do NOT fall, the RELATED SITES section is not being used and this cell is falsified — measurable
directly, because `gq_calls.log` records every wrapper call and the transcripts record every grep.

## Guard against the obvious failure mode

The accuracy risk is that "trust RELATED SITES" makes eg skip real sites the section missed. Check:
per-instance, compare the gold patch's file set against the payload's RELATED SITES file set, on the
DISJOINT pool (`.elig_h30`), before running this on any reported set.

Confirmed, and it's my own error reproduced in mirror image: eg's arm block carries **6 clamp phrases** ("minimal fix", "do not chain more tool calls", "in as FEW turns", "NEVER read a whole file", "Do not re-read", "STOP") while **baseline and cmm carry zero**. I inherited that clamp from `cmm_clamp_prompt` when I built the payload block. So eg was under frugality pressure its comparators didn't have — it stopped 10 turns early and lost 4 resolves.

The principled fix: under `thorough`, **all policy belongs in the shared block; the tool block should be pure capability description.** Implementing:

input.command:
GM=/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-suhaan-devenv/7e3deab1-a028-46d5-9bf1-3318de93a0b6/scratchpad/graphmark/agentic-swebench

src=open(p).read()
new_fn = '''# EG_CAPABILITY_ONLY=1 — the arm block reduced to a pure CAPABILITY DESCRIPTION, with every policy
# sentence removed. Reason, measured on config 7 run 1 (.p2_haiku, thorough family): the shared block
# was byte-identical across arms (md5 verified) but eg's ARM block still carried six frugality clamp
# phrases that baseline and cmm did not have any of -- "minimal fix", "do not chain more tool calls",
# "in as FEW turns", "NEVER read a whole file", "Do not re-read", "STOP". Result: eg ran 29.89 turns
# against baseline's 39.75 and resolved 17/30 against baseline's 21/30. That is the SAME early-stopping
# trade that cost the published clamp round 19 resolves, reproduced in mirror image -- this time the
# unfairness was against eg, and it was mine.
# Design rule this cell establishes: under a family that emits shared_block, the arm block describes
# WHAT THE TOOL IS AND RETURNS and nothing else; ALL policy comes from the shared block, which is
# byte-identical by construction. Each arm keeps exactly one "if it does not land" fallback sentence,
# matching what tool_block's cmm and baseline branches already had.
capability_only_eg_prompt() {  # $1 = wrapper command
  cat <<TXT
A precomputed, deterministic code graph for this repository is available through one command. Use it
INSTEAD OF grep/glob when finding code definitions, implementations, or relationships:
  $1 search "<what you are looking for>"
      ranked hits across the whole repository. For the top-ranked hits it prints the COMPLETE body of
      the enclosing function, verbatim, with its real line numbers, marked complete-symbol; lower
      ranked hits appear as a file:line locator instead. The result also lists RELATED SITES — callers,
      sibling implementations and near-duplicate bodies — and, when it can determine one, a VERIFY
      command for the file you are changing.
  $1 def <Symbol>      the full source of a symbol
  $1 callers <Symbol>  inbound call paths through the graph, file:line and hop per entry
  $1 impact <Symbol>   callers, callees, type consumers, co-change files and siblings in one shot
  $1 grep <regex>      grep mapped onto the enclosing symbol and ranked by hit density
It is deterministic and local: the same query returns the same answer, and it never leaves this repo.
If a search does not land the right code, search again with different words, and prefer the graph's own
grep verb over a shell hunt. But it is one signal, not an oracle: if two searches have not put you on
the right code, fall back to the shell, batched into one call.
TXT
}
'''

assert anchor not in src, "already present"
marker = "# CLAUSE PARITY (2026-07-28, this cell)"
assert marker in src
src = src.replace(marker, new_fn + marker, 1)
# wire it first in tool_block's eg branch
old = '''    eg)
      # EG_EDIT_FROM_PAYLOAD was previously reachable ONLY under PROMPT_FAMILY=briefed'''
new = '''    eg)
      if [ "${EG_CAPABILITY_ONLY:-0}" = 1 ]; then capability_only_eg_prompt "$2"; return; fi
