# Implementation brief — make entire-graph clear −35% tokens on Sonnet

Paste everything below the line into the agent working on `entire-graph`.

---

## What you are doing

Make `entire-graph` cut a Claude-Code-on-**Sonnet** agent's session tokens by **≥35% versus the same
agent with no tool**, at **no loss of resolved issues**, on SWE-bench Multilingual. Sonnet
specifically. Haiku's ceiling is ~−32% and opus/fable are arithmetically closed (see §5) — do not
spend effort there.

Repo: `github.com/entireio/entire-graph`. Work on a branch off `integ/rebase-2026-07-28`. Build with
CGO (tree-sitter). `gofmt`, `go vet`, `go test ./...` must all be clean before you claim anything.

## 1. The cost model you are optimising (fitted, not assumed)

    session_tokens  ≈  T · F  +  G · T(T+1)/2          F ≈ 17,000

`T` = agent turns. `G` = NEW context added per turn, which is then re-read on every later turn — 95.9%
of billed tokens are context replay, so the quadratic term dominates. Fitted from real sessions:

| model | T_base | tokens_base | T_eg | tokens_eg | G_base | G_eg | reads/session (eg) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **sonnet** | **17.1** | **750,532** | **15.7** | **678,732** | **2,969** | **3,150** | **3.2** |
| haiku | 28.0 | 990,744 | 30.9 | 1,276,742 | 1,272 | 1,521 | 7.0 |

Two conclusions that determine the whole design:

1. **G_eg > G_base on every model.** The excess IS the search payload. On sonnet it is 181/turn.
2. **Payload-only fixes cannot reach −35%.** Make the payload completely free (G = G_base) with turns
   unchanged and sonnet lands at **−12.6%**. The target needs **T ≤ 12.9**, i.e. **2.8 turns deleted**
   from 15.7. Sonnet has **3.2 reads/session** available to delete. It fits — barely. That margin is
   the whole project.

## 2. The leverage rule — internalise this, it inverts the obvious instinct

    one agent turn   = 17,000 tokens of fixed cost, plus its replay
    one ~1.5 KB body =    375 tokens, amortised
    ratio            = 45×

**Always spend payload bytes to delete a turn.** Shrinking payloads to save bytes is the wrong
direction and was measured as such. The only reason to shrink the payload is to remove bytes that
buy no turn — see the locator finding.

## 3. Lever A — stop emitting ranks that cannot carry a body

`internal/sem/search_enclosure.go:38`:

    searchEnclosureHeadRanks = 5   // both "never demoted to a locator" AND
                                   // "the only ones eligible for the complete-body upgrade"

`internal/sem/search.go` has `defaultSearchTopK = 10`. **10 > 5, so ranks 6–10 can only ever be
locators** — a path and a line and no code. Verified against the shipped binary on one repo/query:

| `--top-k` | complete bodies | locators | payload |
|---|---|---|---|
| 5 | 3 | 2 | 1,731 B |
| 10 (default) | 3 | 7 | 2,064 B |
| 20 | 3 | **18** | 2,776 B |

Going 20 → 5 keeps **every** body and drops **16 of 18** locators: −38% payload, zero loss of
editable content. Change `defaultSearchTopK` to 5 and state the coupling in the comment: a default
above `searchEnclosureHeadRanks` can only add locators.

Do **not** touch the allocator. `searchEnclosureGrowthBytes = searchEnclosureHeadRanks * 2048` is
sized for exactly five bodies and is independent of the tail, so removing tail bytes cannot starve
the head.

## 4. Lever B — convert locators into bodies (this is where the 2.8 turns come from)

A locator's only actionable use is a `Read`, and a Read is a turn. Measured across three cells:
**80–95% of reads re-open a file the payload already contained** (56/59, 122/147, 98/122). Every
locator you turn into a body removes the read it exists to invite, at 45:1 leverage.

Bodies are capped not by rank but by **enclosure availability** — `searchEnclosure.available()`
requires a known symbol, a readable file, an enclosable kind, and ≤ `defaultSearchEnclosureMaxLines`
(160, `search_enclosure.go:32`). At `--top-k 3` there were still 2 locators and only 1 body, so rank
is not the binding constraint. Widen availability:

- raise `defaultSearchEnclosureMaxLines` (160 → try 320/400); a body 4× the cap still costs ~375
  tokens against a 17,000-token turn
- reconsider `searchEnclosableSymbolKind` (`search_enclosure.go:~87`), which excludes containers.
  A hit inside a class that is not a method currently gets no body. Do not return whole 3,000-line
  classes — bound it by lines, not by kind, where you can

Instrument as you go: emit the per-payload counts of bodies vs locators and the reason each locator
failed to upgrade (unknown symbol / not enclosable / over cap / unreadable). **The distribution of
those reasons tells you which sub-lever is worth pulling.** Get that before changing constants.

## 5. Do not attempt these — already measured, with numbers

| idea | result | why it is dead |
|---|---|---|
| discipline paragraph in eg's prompt only | −18.9% → **+26.9%** when removed | it is cheating; it killed the published 54.9% and 31.6% |
| payload byte budget 24576 → 16384 | ceiling **4.27%** | cannot close a 20-point gap |
| tool-optional ("skip when the task is easy") | **+45.0%** [+18.6,+79.5] | the model cannot predict when it needs the index; it explores and spends more turns |
| a `COMPLETE BODY:` notice above head bodies | **+10.5%** (n.s.), turns 32.3→34.3 | no effect on reads |
| raising top-k for recall | payload recall up, agent tokens worse | recall without an agent ≠ tokens with one |
| bodies-only (suppress locators) | rejected | locators are missing-enclosure hits; suppressing DROPS real match locations |
| chasing opus / fable | closed | at G parity fable is **−2.9%**; opus eg has **0.4 reads/session** — no turns to delete |

## 6. Rules you may not break

1. **No arm-specific prompt advantage.** Two prior headline numbers died to this. Any prompt text
   must be byte-identical across baseline / eg / cmm, verified in the emitted `prompt.txt`, not in
   the script. Ship config and code changes, not prompt changes.
2. **Symmetric comparison tool config.** If you change eg's visible hit count, set
   `CMM_SNIPPET_TOP` to match.
3. **3 replicates minimum.** Run-to-run noise on a byte-identical configuration is **±20%** total
   tokens; MDE at n=29 is 31%. A single run cannot see the effect you are chasing.
4. **Report total AND paired geomean, named.** They differ by ~15 points on identical data.
5. Never quote a number without its n and CI.

## 7. Definition of done

Cell A (current default) vs Cell B (your change), sonnet, 20 nested instances, 3 replicates, matched
prompts.

By the brief's own 45:1 leverage rule that's a bad trade — a locator that names the fix site *prevents* turns.

So the real prize is the 58–62% of reads that re-open an already-printed body. Testing whether those reads want lines *outside* the printed span — which would make them legitimate and point at a concrete fix:

  inside          6    3.8%

  no_range       13    8.1%
  TOTAL         160

outside    = wants lines the body did not cover (imports, another symbol) -> LEGITIMATE; the fix is

**This is the answer, and it inverts both levers.** Only 3.8% of those reads are waste — **80% legitimately want lines the printed body doesn't cover**: imports/file head (body at 66-87, agent reads 1-100), the neighbourhood around the body (body 198-211 → reads 190-299), or a different symbol entirely (body 28-55 → reads 266-283).

The agent isn't disobeying; the payload is too *narrow*. Quantifying the exact shape so the fix is derived, not guessed:

input.description: Quantify what would prevent each outside read

result.output:
THE 'outside' READS — what would have prevented each one?  (n=128)

  file_head(<=20)                      20   15.6%
  adjacent(<=40 lines from body)       53   41.4%
  adjacent(41-160)                     30   23.4%
  far(>160)                            25   19.5%

  gap to nearest printed body: median 42 lines, mean 134
  requested window width      : median 50 lines, mean 82

DESIGN IMPLICATION (derived, not guessed):
  file_head  -> the agent needs the file's imports/header to write a correct edit. Cheap and bounded:
                an import block is tens of lines and is the SAME for every hit in that file.
  adjacent   -> the agent needs the code immediately around the body. A wider context window on head
                hits buys these back at ~375 tokens each against a 17,000-token turn (45:1).
  far        -> a different symbol in the same file; that is what a container map indexes, but an
                index still costs the Read. Only a body prevents the turn.

# entire-graph vs the ≥35% token gate — iteration 9 (terminal)

**Gate:** accuracy ≥ baseline AND tokens < baseline AND tokens < cmm AND tokens ≤ −35% vs baseline,
on 5/300 fable, 10/300 opus, 20/300 sonnet, 30/300 haiku. No cheating.

Iteration 9 supersedes 1–8. It is terminal because it replaces "we have not found the lever yet"
with two proofs about why three of the four tiers cannot be won, and a measured expected value for
the only change the data actually licenses.

---

## 0. Verdict

| leg | result |
|---|---|
| no cheating | **PASS.** 0 leaks in all 12 cells; 2 bypass attempts, both `exit 86`. One was the *baseline*. |
| tokens < cmm | **PASS on all 4 tiers** (billed_new −19.6% / −10.3% / −32.2% / −24.2%). |
| tokens < baseline | **haiku only.** |
| tokens ≤ −35% | **haiku only, and only on `total_tokens` (−37.8%).** Not on `billed_new` (−18.2%). |
| accuracy ≥ baseline | **sonnet yes (16 vs 15).** haiku baseline 10/29, cmm 10/29, eg 7/19 + 10 re-grades pending. |

**The gate is not passed, and §1 and §2 prove it cannot be as specified.**

## 1. PROOF A — a ≥35% `billed_new` win is arithmetically impossible on every tier

A locate tool can only displace localization work. It cannot touch the system prompt, the tool
schemas, the conversation prefix, or the model's own output. Measured tool_result bytes per session,
converted at 4 B/token:

| tier | baseline billed_new | explore+Read tokens | **share** | eg measured |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| fable | 32,034 | 2,552 | **8.0%** | +10.5% |
| opus | 29,203 | 3,102 | **10.6%** | +38.2% |
| sonnet | 34,228 | 3,972 | **11.6%** | +15.9% |
| haiku | 49,947 | 8,700 | **17.4%** | **−18.2%** |

The `share` column is the ceiling for a **perfect, zero-cost** locate tool. **eg on haiku measured
−18.2% against a 17.4% ceiling — 104% of it**, because it also removed build/test churn. There is no
headroom left on this axis, and no tier's ceiling is within 17 points of −35%.

`total_tokens` can exceed the ceiling because turn savings compound through per-turn prefix re-reads
(cache_read, billed at ~1/10). That is the only metric on which −35% is reachable, and haiku clears
it: **−37.8% [−56.2, −11.1]**.

## 2. PROOF B — three of the four tiers are below the resolution needed to see the effect

From `entire-graph/AGENTS.md`, measured on byte-identical re-runs: run-to-run noise on total tokens
is **±20%**, and the minimum detectable effect at 80% power is **31% at n=29, 59% at n=10, 93% at
n=5**. The goal's tier sizes are 5 / 10 / 20 / 30.

**A −35% effect is not detectable at n=5 (MDE 93%) or n=10 (MDE 59%).** fable and opus cannot
establish the gate even if the effect were real; haiku (n=30) is the only adequately-powered tier,
and sonnet (n=20) is marginal. Every fable/opus/sonnet number in iteration 9 is a single run and
must be read as direction, not result.

## 3. The mechanism, settled

eg displaces exploration on every tier — but only haiku converts that into a net saving:

| tier | explore calls base→eg | tool_result bytes base→eg | net |
|---|---|---|---|
| haiku | 20.90 → 13.47 | 42,422 → 33,769 | **−8,653** |
| fable | 6.20 → 3.80 | 11,990 → 13,590 | +1,600 |
| sonnet | 11.00 → 7.70 | 20,031 → 26,269 | +6,238 |
| opus | 7.10 → 5.10 | 15,514 → 22,138 | +6,624 |

On opus the payload is **purely additive**: explore bytes *rose* (4,776→5,637), Read stayed flat
(7,633→7,825), build rose (2,236→3,348). Baseline on opus spends only 7.1 explore calls / 15.5 KB —
there is nothing to displace, so a 4.6 KB payload is pure cost. That is the whole per-model gradient.

## 4. Levers measured and REJECTED in iteration 9 (each with its killing number)

| lever | verdict | number |
|---|---|---|
| **byte budget 24576 → 12288 / 8192 / 6144** | dead | budget **is not binding**: byte-identical on 27/30 at 12288. Real payload is 4,310 B mean. Gold recall flat 22/30 down to 8192; at 6144 complete bodies collapse 3.10 → 1.34. Cannot save bytes never spent. |
| **Lever A — `defaultSearchTopK` 10 → 5** | **REJECT** | gold file sits at ranks 6–8 on **5/30 = 17%** of instances. Cutting to 5 removes the only mention of the fix site on 17% of instances to save ~83 tokens against a 17,000-token turn. The brief's "zero loss of editable content" is true of *bodies* and false of *locations*. |
| **Lever B — locators → bodies** | **insufficient** | of sonnet's 41 in-payload reads, **30 already had a complete body**. Locator-only reads are 11 = **0.55/session**. Sonnet needs **2.8 turns** deleted. Lever B covers 20% of the requirement. |
| **on-demand `show <id>`** | dead | no `show` subcommand exists; it would trade payload bytes (already only ~1,080 tok/call) for an extra Read turn at 45:1 against. |
| **verify-command derivation** | already shipped | the `VERIFY` block exists on `integ/rebase-2026-07-28`. Not a new lever. |

## 5. What the read data actually licenses — the one derived change

80–88% of eg's Reads re-open a file the payload already listed, and 58–62% re-open a file whose
**complete body was already printed**. That looks like disobedience. It is not:

| what the read asked for | n=128 | share |
|---|---|---|
| lines the payload already printed (pure waste) | 6 | **3.8%** |
| **lines OUTSIDE the printed body** | **128** | **80.0%** |
| whole file despite holding the body | 13 | 8.1% |

The payload is too **narrow**, not too large. Breaking down the 128:

| what would have prevented it | share | fix |
|---|---|---|
| file head / imports (`≤20`) | 15.6% | emit the top hit's file header/import block once per file, bounded ≤1 KB |
| within 40 lines of the body | 41.4% | context margin on the rank-1 body |
| 41–160 lines away | 23.4% | wider margin; cost grows faster than benefit |
| >160 lines away | 19.5% | a different symbol — only another body prevents it |

Median requested window is **50 lines**; median gap to the nearest printed body is **42 lines**.

**Recommended change (positive expected value, bounded):** emit the top hit's import/header block,
capped at ~30 lines / 1 KB, deduplicated per file. Cost ≈ 1 KB × 4.5 calls = 1,100 tok/session.
Prevents 15.6% of 128 reads ≈ 0.31 turns/session ≈ 5,300 tok. **Net ≈ −4,200 tok/session.**
**Falsifier:** if `Read` calls with `offset ≤ 20` do not fall, the header was not what those reads
wanted and the block must be removed.

**Honest ceiling on this family:** preventing *every* file-head and adjacent read (57% of 128) is
1.12 turns/session — **−7% turns on sonnet**, not −35%. The derived change is a real improvement and
is not a route to the gate.

## 6. Integrity ledger for iteration 9

- Prompts matched: eg 6 clamp phrases / 0 task-strategy clauses; baseline 6 / 0. Baseline's block is
  **longer** (253 vs 239 words), so its prefix replay is dearer — conservative for eg.
- Leak audit, all 12 cells: **0 leaked**. Two bypass attempts (`git -C … stash` on *baseline*,
  `git -C … log` on eg) both returned `Exit code 86`. `git apply/am` and absolute-path git: **0 calls
  in 0 sessions**, so the older guard used by these cells is behaviourally identical to the hardened
  one on `graph-savings-iterate`.
- Cost validity: `total_cost_usd` re-derived from `modelUsage` per model. Helper-model spend is
  ≤0.7% of total and equal across arms; target-model-only and all-model deltas agree within 0.2 pt.
- Tier sets are **nested** (fable 5 ⊂ opus 10 ⊂ sonnet 20 ⊂ haiku 30), so tiers compare on identical
  instances. The screen set `.elig_val30` is disjoint from all of them.

## 7. Corrections issued in iteration 9

1. **"The matched clamp cost eg 12 resolves" — RETRACTED.** That rested on `P4hkeg_r1` 7/30, a cell
   with **10 grading errors** (409 container-name clashes from a grader I killed; 404 images my
   `docker image prune -af` removed). It is 7 of **19 completed**. Baseline under the same clamp fell
   18/30 → 10/29, so the clamp costs **both** arms; it is fair, not eg-specific.
2. **"eg is not using the graph on opus" — WRONG.** It is: explore falls 7.10 → 5.10. The cost is
   that the saving is smaller than the payload.
3. A blanket `docker rm -f` of `sweb.eval*` containers **killed a live grade at 18/29**. Container
   cleanup is now scoped to a single `run_id`.

input.content:
# The achievable frontier for the ≥35% token gate — three proofs

Measured by the Claude Code session, 2026-07-29. Companion to `CLAUDE-FINDINGS-FOR-GATE.md` and
`CLAUDE-IDEAS-ALL-MODELS.md`, and a **correction** to parts of both.

**Gate:** accuracy ≥ baseline AND tokens < baseline AND tokens < cmm AND tokens ≤ −35% vs baseline,
on 5 fable / 10 opus / 20 sonnet / 30 haiku.

Config 9 = matched frugality clamp (verified in the RENDERED prompts: eg 6 clamp phrases / 0
task-strategy clauses; baseline 6 / 0; baseline's block is *longer*, 253 vs 239 words, so its prefix
replay is dearer — conservative for eg) + `EG_TOPK=10` + `EG_NO_SNIPCAP=1`. Tier sets are **nested**
(fable 5 ⊂ opus 10 ⊂ sonnet 20 ⊂ haiku 30), so all tiers compare on identical instances.

---

## 0. Result

| tier | turns | billed_new vs base | total_tok vs base | billed_new vs cmm | resolves |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **haiku** n=30 | **−35.1%** \* | −18.2% | **−37.8%** \* | **−24.2%** \* | base 10/29, cmm 10/29, eg 7/19 (+10 re-grades) |
| fable n=5 | **−25.2%** \* | +10.5% | −12.3% | −19.6% | 4 / 4 / 4 |
| sonnet n=20 | −8.2% | **+15.9%** \* | +4.0% | **−32.2%** \* | **eg 16 vs base 15** |
| opus n=10 | +2.5% | **+38.2%** \* | +24.0% | −10.3% | ungraded |

\* = 95% CI (paired geometric mean, bootstrap) excludes zero. **eg beats cmm on every tier.**
`billed_new` = input+cache_creation+output; `total_tokens` adds cache_read, which bills at ~1/10.

**Gate not passed.** The three proofs below say it cannot be, as specified.

## 1. PROOF A — ≥35% on `billed_new` is arithmetically impossible on every tier

A locate tool can only displace localization. It cannot touch the system prompt, the tool schemas,
the conversation prefix, or the model's own output. Measured `tool_result` bytes per session at
4 B/token:

| tier | baseline billed_new | explore+Read tokens | **ceiling** | eg measured |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| fable | 32,034 | 2,552 | **8.0%** | +10.5% |
| opus | 29,203 | 3,102 | **10.6%** | +38.2% |
| sonnet | 34,228 | 3,972 | **11.6%** | +15.9% |
| haiku | 49,947 | 8,700 | **17.4%** | **−18.2%** |

`ceiling` is what a **perfect, zero-cost** locate tool could remove. **eg on haiku is at 104% of its
ceiling** (it also removed build/test churn). No tier's ceiling is within 17 points of −35%.

`total_tokens` can exceed the ceiling because turn savings compound through per-turn prefix re-reads.
That is the only metric on which −35% is reachable, and haiku clears it at **−37.8%**.

## 2. PROOF B — three of the four tier sizes cannot resolve the effect

`entire-graph/AGENTS.md`, measured on byte-identical re-runs: run-to-run noise on total tokens is
**±20%**; MDE at 80% power is **31% at n=29, 59% at n=10, 93% at n=5**.

**At n=5 (fable) and n=10 (opus) a −35% effect is undetectable even if real.** haiku (n=30) is the
only adequately powered tier; sonnet (n=20) is marginal. Treat every fable/opus/sonnet figure here as
direction, not result.

## 3. PROOF C — the only remaining token pool is verification, and it buys accuracy

81% of turns are post-first-edit. The baseline **never receives a `VERIFY` block**, so it is the
instance-difficulty control. Same 65 instances, split on whether eg's payload carried `VERIFY:`:

| arm | VERIFY group | turns | build calls |
|---|---|---|---|
| eg | present (n=36) | 20.44 | 3.31 |
| eg | absent (n=29) | **13.86** | **0.59** |
| baseline | present-group | 23.47 | 3.08 |
| baseline | absent-group | 20.34 | 1.48 |

- turn gap: eg **+47.5%** vs baseline **+15.4%** → `VERIFY` adds ≈ **+32 pp of turns**
- build gap: eg **+463.9%** vs baseline +107.9% → the block is what makes the agent verify at all

**eg is −32% turns where it skips verification and only −12.9% where it verifies.** The big token
wins come from not verifying — the same behaviour that cost the published config its accuracy
(131 vs 150, p=0.0204; zero builds on 22 of 31 paired losses).

**So raising `VERIFY` coverage (measured at only 50%: 3/5, 6/10, 12/20, 15/30) would *increase*
tokens.** It is an accuracy lever, not a token lever. Token saving and resolve rate are one variable
— how much the agent verifies — and the gate asks for both ends of it at once.

## 4. Levers rejected here, each with its killing number

| lever | verdict | number |
|---|---|---|
| byte budget 24576 → 12288/8192/6144 | dead | budget **not binding** — byte-identical on 27/30 at 12288; real payload 4,310 B. Gold recall flat 22/30 down to 8192; at 6144 bodies collapse 3.10 → 1.34 |
| `defaultSearchTopK` 10 → 5 | **reject** | gold file sits at rank 6–8 on **5/30 = 17%**; cutting to 5 deletes the only mention of the fix site to save ~83 tokens against a 17,000-token turn |
| locators → bodies | insufficient | of sonnet's 41 in-payload reads **30 already had a complete body**; locator-only reads are **0.55/session** against the **2.8 turns** sonnet needs |
| on-demand `show <id>` | dead | no such subcommand; trades ~1,080 tok/call of payload for an extra Read turn at 45:1 against |
| raise `VERIFY` coverage | **inverts** | Proof C: +32 pp turns |

## 5. What the read data does license (net-positive, bounded)

80–88% of eg's Reads re-open a file the payload already listed; 58–62% re-open one whose complete
body was printed. That is **not** disobedience — of those reads only **3.8%** ask for lines already
printed, while **80% ask for lines outside the body**: file head/imports 15.6%, within 40 lines
41.4%, 41–160 lines 23.4%, >160 lines 19.5% (median gap 42 lines, median window 50 lines).

**The payload is too narrow, not too large.** Recommended: emit the top hit's import/header block,
≤30 lines / ≤1 KB, deduplicated per file. Cost ≈1,100 tok/session; prevents ≈0.31 turns ≈5,300 tok;
**net ≈ −4,200 tok/session**. **Falsifier:** if `Read` calls with `offset ≤ 20` do not fall, remove it.
Honest ceiling for this whole family: preventing *every* head+adjacent read is 1.12 turns/session =
**−7% turns on sonnet**. A real improvement; not a route to the gate.

## 6. Corrections to my own earlier claims

1. **`SAME-CONCEPT LITERALS` "never fires (0/65)" — WRONG, my detector's fault.** The renderer writes

Decisive. Rank utility on sonnet:

| rank | files shown | had body | later Read | later **Edited** |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **1** | 24 | 19 | **62%** | **54%** |
| 2 | 15 | 9 | 27% | 20% |
| 3 | 9 | 4 | **0%** | 11% |
| 4 | 15 | 10 | 7% | 7% |
| 5 | 13 | 7 | **0%** | **0%** |
| 6–10 | 77 | 0 | 8% | 3% |

`searchEnclosureHeadRanks = 5` buys **21 complete bodies at ranks 3–5 that are read 0–7% of the time**. That's ~43% of the body spend wasted, while rank 1 — read 62%, edited 54% — is the only rank that pays and is too narrow to prevent its own reads.

So the sonnet fix is: **stop paying for bodies at ranks 3–5, spend it widening rank 1.** Implementing it as tunable options rather than changed constants, so haiku's current behaviour isn't regressed:

No — and this is a real defect that invalidates the run I just started. Checking the harness's own claim against the product:

`shipped_eg_prompt`'s comment says it is *"the block entire-graph publishes in AGENTS.md under 'The measured-best agent prompt (copy-paste this)' — i.e. exactly what the vendor tells users to give their agent."* **It isn't.** Diffing against the real inject:

| the real AGENTS.md inject says | the harness's "shipped" block says |
|---|---|
| "go straight to the top hit and **edit from the body it printed** — do not re-read the file" | "**open the top hit's file with your native Read tool** (pass a line range)" |
| **SAME-CONCEPT LITERALS** — "This IS your sweep… do not grep for them" | absent |
| **VERIFY** — "Run it ONCE when your edits are in" | absent |
| **CLOSED-SET WARNING** — "Add the missing arm before you stop" | absent |
| "Ask for them **ALL IN ONE MESSAGE**" (batching) | absent |
| (AGENTS.md calls chaining `search→def→callers` "the #1 measured token waste") | advertises `def`, `callers`, `impact`, `grep` |

Three consequences, and they're not minor:

1. **It mandates the Read that the product tells the agent to skip.** That directly manufactures the read-redundancy I measured — 80–88% of eg's Reads re-open a file the payload already contained. That cost is the *harness's*, not the tool's.
2. **The agent is never told how to use blocks that do fire** — `SAME-CONCEPT LITERAL` 11/20 and `VERIFY` 12/20 on sonnet. Those bytes are paid for and unusable.
3. **It makes my rank-1 margin untestable.** The margin's whole purpose is to remove a follow-up read — but this prompt *instructs* a read regardless. So the sonnet run I just launched cannot measure the change I built.

Right — and now I can see exactly what "all of it" is. The canonical inject is the `agentGuide` const in `internal/cli/agents.go` (175 lines); `init-agents` writes **that** into a project's AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md, so it *is* what a real agent reads. `agent-guide` prints it.

So the fix is: the harness should read the eg block from `$EG agent-guide` instead of hardcoding a copy. Then AGENTS.md/`agentGuide` is the one source of truth and drift is impossible by construction. Implementing that:

#   - the guide says "edit from the body it printed - do NOT re-read the file"; shipped_eg_prompt
#     instead instructs "open the top hit's file with your native Read tool". That single inversion
#     MANUFACTURES the follow-up read the product exists to remove (measured: 80-88% of eg's Reads

#   - the guide's three round-trip-replacing blocks (SAME-CONCEPT LITERALS / VERIFY / CLOSED-SET

# it from the binary makes drift impossible: there is one string, the product owns it, and the
# harness records its hash so a change is visible in the manifest instead of invisible in a diff.

# This measures THE PRODUCT AS SHIPPED. It is deliberately NOT the matched-policy control: the guide

  # wrapper once. This is the only harness-authored sentence in the block.
  printf '%s\\n' "In this environment the command is: $1"

Yes — you're right, and that's the correct fix. Pushed as `f8e731a`.

## Answering your question straight

**graphmark is clean — I wasn't.** The harness *does* contain a faithful copy of the real inject (`ops_clamp_eg_prompt`, `PROMPT_FAMILY=briefed`, exactly as AGENTS.md names). I ran `EG_SHIPPED_PROMPT=1` under `PROMPT_FAMILY=vendor`, which is a **stale clone** whose own comment claims to be "exactly what the vendor tells users" and isn't:

| real inject (`agent-guide`) | the stale block I used |
|---|---|
| "**edit from the body it printed** — do NOT re-read the file" | "**open the top hit's file with your native Read tool**" |
| SAME-CONCEPT LITERALS / VERIFY / CLOSED-SET WARNING | all three absent |
| "Ask for them **ALL IN ONE MESSAGE**" | absent |
| calls `def`/`callers`/`impact` chaining the #1 token waste | advertises them |

**This materially corrects my own reporting.** That one inversion *manufactures* the read the product exists to remove — so my headline finding "80–88% of eg's Reads re-open a payload file, so the payload is too narrow" is substantially an artifact of the harness telling the agent to read. The rank-1 margin I built and PR'd was designed against a problem the prompt created. It may still help, but its justification is now weaker than I stated.

I stopped the sonnet run at 14/13 of 30 rather than spend the rest of the $27 — under that prompt the margin is untestable, since the agent is *instructed* to Read regardless.

`EG_GUIDE_FROM_BINARY=1` now sets the eg block to `$ENTIRE_GRAPH agent-guide` **verbatim** — the same 175-line string `init-agents` writes into a project's AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md — and hashes it into each session (`eg_guide.md5`, currently `377dd17c`). One string, owned by the product. Drift becomes impossible instead of silent.

## One thing you should decide, because it changes what the number means

The guide carries *operating policy*, not just capability. So:

- **Product-as-shipped** (guide vs bare baseline): answers "does entire-graph save a real user tokens?" Asymmetric by design — the asymmetry *is* the product.
- **Index-only** (matched policy both arms): answers "does the graph itself save tokens?"

Both are legitimate; conflating them is precisely what killed the 54.9% and 31.6% claims. I've wired the switch for the first and left the matched-policy control intact, and I'd run **both** and label them rather than pick one silently.

Yes — and that number is the honest headline, so let me not dress it up.

## Exact accounting

**entire-graph PR #70 — 217 lines added**

| kind | lines |

| kind | lines |
|---|---|
| analysis tooling | 760 |
| findings docs | 486 |
| harness/tools fixes | 153 |

So: **~80 executable lines of product change**, ~1,600 total.

## Why it's that small, stated plainly

Almost every lever I tested was **refuted with a number**, and a refuted lever correctly produces zero lines of code:

| lever | why no code shipped |
|---|---|
| byte budget 24576→8192 | budget was never binding — byte-identical on 27/30 |
| `--top-k` 10→5 | deletes the gold file's only mention on 17% of instances |
| locators→bodies | covers 0.55 of the 2.8 turns sonnet needs |
| raise `VERIFY` coverage | *inverts* — +32pp turns |
| inject the whole `agent-guide` | +133% usd, +175% total_tokens |
| Go interface-method extraction | broke a test, CONTAINS −764 |

What survived screening was genuinely two small things: bound where bodies get planned, and pad rank 1. That's 80 lines.

There's also a structural reason there wasn't a big feature to add: **eg on haiku already measures −18.2% billed_new against a 17.4% arithmetic ceiling — 104% of what any locate tool could ever remove.** The gap on sonnet/opus isn't a missing capability; it's that those baselines barely explore (7.1 and 11.0 explore calls vs haiku's 20.9), so there's nothing to displace.

The largest single thing I found wasn't a graph improvement at all — it was that the benchmark's `EG_SHIPPED_PROMPT` block **inverts the product's core instruction** and omits all three payload blocks, so every cell measured with it understates entire-graph. That's 153 lines of harness fix and it invalidates part of my own earlier analysis.

One PR replacing the five-PR stack (#66 → main, plus #67/#68/#69/#70 stacked on `integ/rebase-2026-07-28`). Those branches had **diverged** — `integ/measure-2026-07-28` was 55 commits ahead of main while `integ/rebase-2026-07-28` was 50, and none of the four stacked branches was contained in either — so reviewing them separately meant reviewing a tree nobody could build. This branch is the union: **71 commits ahead of `main`**, merged cleanly, built and tested as one thing.

## Verified on this exact tree

- `gofmt -l` clean
- `go build ./...` clean
- `go vet ./internal/...` clean
- `go test ./...` — all 6 packages pass (`cli`, `sem`, `bench`, `cmd/graph-bench`, `filedigest`, `gitutil`)

Smoke-tested **inside a linked git worktree**, which is the condition that made `integ/rebase-2026-07-28` return zero results (`read ignore file … not a directory`) and would have silently voided any benchmark run on it:

| config | payload | complete bodies |
|---|---|---|
| defaults | 4,310 B | 3 |
| `--body-head-ranks 2 --enclosure-context-lines 40` | 7,265 B | 2 |

## What it contains

**Retrieval stack** (was #66): complete-symbol payloads, related sites, literal clusters, bounded working-tree listing.

**Correctness fixes** (were #67/#68/#69):
- search returned **zero results in every git worktree** — the single highest-impact bug here, since agent sessions run in linked worktrees
- committed-tree caches keyed on the resolved file cap; records cache keyed on repo identity
- nested `.gitignore` honoured in the vendored-directory heuristic; default cache dir

**Snippet allocation** (was #70) — two opt-in `SearchOptions`, `0` = today's behaviour byte-for-byte:

| option | flag | effect |
|---|---|---|
| `BodyHeadRanks` | `--body-head-ranks` | caps how deep the **complete-body** upgrade reaches, independently of the locator head |
| `EnclosureContextLines` | `--enclosure-context-lines` | pads the **rank-1** body N lines each side |

Measured rank utility (sonnet, 20 SWE-bench Multilingual instances) — of the files a payload showed, how often the agent later touched them:

| rank | shown | later Read | later **Edited** |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 24 | **62%** | **54%** |
| 2 | 15 | 27% | 20% |
| 3 | 9 | **0%** | 11% |
| 4 | 15 | 7% | 7% |
| 5 | 13 | **0%** | **0%** |

`searchEnclosureHeadRanks = 5` therefore buys **21 complete bodies at ranks 3–5 that are read 0–7% of the time**, and their bytes replay on every later turn. The body head and locator head must move **separately**, because the gold file sits at **rank 6–8 on 17% of instances** — shortening the *ranking* loses fix sites, which is why cutting `--top-k` to 5 was measured and rejected. A locator costs ~70 B; a body ~1 kB.

Screened on 30 disjoint instances, no model calls: `--body-head-ranks 2 --enclosure-context-lines 40` is **byte-neutral (+2.4%)** at **identical gold recall (22/30)** and identical gold-body/top-1-body coverage — dropping the unread bodies pays for the rank-1 margin. `--body-head-ranks 1` is **not viable** (loses 6 gold bodies, including at ranks 1 and 2).

**Doc/code drift fix:** the payload prints `SAME-CONCEPT LITERAL` while the guide, AGENTS.md and the guide's own test said `SAME-CONCEPT LITERALS`. The guide *tells an agent to look for the block by name*. Measured cost: a grep-based audit of 65 real sessions reported the block firing **0/65** when it actually fired **43/65**. Fixed structurally — `sem` exports `LiteralClusterBlockName`, the renderer builds its header from it, and the guide's test asserts that constant instead of a hand-typed string.

## Caveat I want on the record

The rank-1 **margin's** justification is weaker than the rank-utility finding. "80% of reads want lines outside the printed body" was measured while the benchmark harness was *instructing* the agent to open the file — the harness's `EG_SHIPPED_PROMPT` block inverts this repo's own guidance ("edit from the body it printed"). The rank-utility result is unaffected (it is about which files get acted on), but the margin needs re-validation under the faithful inject. Both options default to off, so nothing ships on the weaker claim. Harness-side fixes are in entirehq/graphmark#55.

Also refuted, so it is not retried: injecting this repo's whole `agent-guide` as the agent prompt — sonnet 30, paired n=29, turns **+102.4%** [+54.5,+163.3], usd **+133.0%**, total_tokens **+175.8%**. The guide is a reference manual; handing an agent the manual makes it explore the tool, which the guide itself calls the #1 measured token waste.

input.description: Research prior art on agentic retrieval
input.prompt:
You are researching prior art to find CONCRETE, implementable techniques that reduce an AI coding agent's token usage when it has a code-search/retrieval tool. Output caveman-terse: claim + source + how to implement. No prose padding.

## The problem, precisely
A local code-graph search tool (`entire-graph`) returns a ranked payload (file:line + source snippets, top-5 as complete function bodies, plus blocks: same-concept literals, a derived test/verify command, a closed-set/enum warning, related sites, covering test). An agent (Claude Code) gets it and fixes a bug.

Measured facts we must respect:
- Session cost ≈ turns × replayed context. 95%+ of billed tokens are context REPLAY, so ONE extra agent turn ≈ 17,000 tokens, while 1KB of extra payload ≈ 250 tokens amortised. **Spending payload bytes to delete a turn is ~45:1 favourable.** Shrinking payloads is therefore usually the WRONG direction.
- The tool already wins where the baseline flails (weak models, long sessions). It LOSES on strong models (sonnet/opus/fable) where the baseline localises in ~7-11 shell calls, because the payload is additive there.
- Post-first-edit work is ~81% of turns (build/test/verify/sweep). Localisation is only ~8-17% of billed tokens. So pure "find the file faster" has a hard ceiling.

## What to find
Search the web and read real sources (papers, engineering blogs, open-source code) for techniques that:
1. Reduce agent TURNS (not payload bytes) in code-editing loops. Batching independent reads/edits, speculative context, one-shot multi-edit, dependency-free parallel tool calls.
2. Make retrieved context SUFFICIENT so the agent does not follow up with reads: how much surrounding context, imports/headers, type definitions, call sites. Any measured numbers on "context sufficiency".
3. Reduce build/test/verify churn: deriving the correct narrow test command, cached test selection, test impact analysis.
4. How comparable tools do it — look at real implementations: **aider's repo-map** (tree-sitter + PageRank ranking, token budget), **Cline/Roo context management**, **Cursor codebase indexing**, **Sourcegraph Cody context**, **Augment Code**, **SWE-agent / OpenHands / Agentless** (Agentless is notable: localisation → repair without agentic search), **CodeRAG / RepoGraph / GraphCodeBERT** style repo-graph retrieval papers, **SWE-bench** leaderboard write-ups that report token cost.
5. Anything with MEASURED token/turn reductions on SWE-bench or SWE-bench-Multilingual. Prefer numbers over claims.

## Rules
- Prefer primary sources: papers with numbers, repos with code, engineering posts with measurements. Name the source for every claim.
- Explicitly flag anything that is marketing with no measurement.
- For each technique: is it a TURN reducer or a BYTE reducer? Turn reducers matter ~45x more.
- Note anything that specifically helps on STRONG models where the baseline is already efficient — that is our failing case.

## Output format (strict)
```
TECHNIQUE <n>: <name>
  source: <url / paper / repo>
  measured: <numbers, or NONE>
  turn-or-byte: TURN | BYTE
  helps-strong-models: yes/no + why
  implement-here: <how it maps onto a ranked-payload code-search tool>
```
Then `TOP 5 FOR OUR CASE:` ranked, with why. Then `DEAD ENDS:` techniques whose own numbers say they will not help us. Do NOT write code.

input.command:
cd /Users/suhaan/devenv/eg-consolidated
rtk git add -A internal/ && rtk git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
search: a head rank with no enclosable callable returns a read window, not a locator

New opt-in SearchOptions.HeadWindowLines / --head-window-lines N (0 = today's behaviour exactly).
When a HEAD rank has no enclosable callable -- an unenclosable container kind, a body past the
160-line cap, a hit outside its own recorded symbol span, a document or template -- it now comes back
as a bounded read window centred on the hit instead of a two-line locator.

WHY, measured over 79 real agent sessions across 5 benchmark cells:
  - the gold file was present in the payload as a LOCATOR ONLY, carrying zero code, in 20 of 74
    sessions; 24 of those at rank <= 3
  - 61 post-search Reads targeted a ranked file that carried no code at all
  - a rank-1 hit showing two lines is an instruction to spend a turn opening the file: ~17,000 tokens
    to recover what ~2 kB of window would have carried
Three independent investigations converged on this: session-log mining ("61% of ranked hits carry zero
code"), a strong-model diagnosis ("ship the code, not the address" -- 24/59 opus post-tool calls exist
only to fetch a body the payload already named), and asking agents directly what blocked them (9/9
named "the body of a symbol the payload NAMED but showed no code for"). Prior art agrees: a comparable
graph tool beat grep 10x on tokens yet lost 9pp of answer quality, and its own paper names omission of
line-level source as the primary cause.

HONESTY OF THE SIGNAL. A window is readable code but NOT a whole callable, so it carries a new
`head-window` signal and NEVER `complete-symbol` -- that signal is the promise "you need no follow-up
read", and a window cannot make it. stats.complete_symbol_snippets still counts complete bodies only;
the allocator tracks windows separately, scores them at 0.25x a body at the same rank (so a plan that
completes a body is always preferred over one that merely widens the same rank), and a plan that
delivered only windows still counts as having bought something.

Window width is 60 lines, taken from what the agents actually asked for: over 128 post-search reads of
a payload file the MEDIAN requested window was 50 lines and the median gap from the printed body was
42 lines. A window only ever ADDS readable lines -- it is refused when the ranker's snippet is already
at least as wide, and it clamps to the file rather than running off either end.

SCREENED on 30 disjoint instances, no model calls, $0:

  config                          bytes   bodies  code hits  gold recall  gold has CODE  code-less gold
  defaults                        4,310    3.10      3.10       22/30         14/30        8 (36%)
  --head-window-lines 60          4,784    3.07      3.40       22/30         16/30        6 (27%)
  + --type-card                   5,051    3.07      3.40       22/30         16/30        6 (27%)
  + --top-k 20                    5,856    3.07      3.40       26/30         16/30       10

Two code-less golds become readable code and no instance regresses. Complete-body count is unchanged
(3.10 -> 3.07), confirming the window only fills ranks a body could never have occupied. --top-k 20 is
orthogonal and additive: it recovers 4 golds that were invisible at k=10 (one sits at rank 13), which
is why it is worth its bytes even though those arrive as locators.

Tests pin the contract: a window must be marked as a window, must never claim complete-symbol, must
carry head-window, must be a verbatim slice, must not shrink an already-wider snippet, and
windowLines=0 must reproduce the old behaviour exactly. gofmt, go vet and go test ./... clean.
EOF

search: FILE OUTLINE — the other symbols in the files the payload already named

New opt-in block (--file-outline, SearchOptions.IncludeFileOutline; off by default). For up to the top
3 ranked files it emits one line per navigable symbol: `start-end kind name`, with `*` marking the
symbol the hit lies in. An INDEX, never source — a payload that printed a body does not pay for a
second copy of it.

WHY, measured over 79 real agent sessions:
  - 77 targeted single-file greps landed on a file the payload had ALREADY named
  - 35 of those were immediately followed by a Read of that same file: a grep->read pair, two turns
    spent answering "what else is in here"
  - reads that follow a payload file land a MEDIAN 109 lines from anything the payload printed, and
    47 of 53 land inside ANOTHER symbol the graph already indexes in that same file
The information was already in the graph and simply was not emitted. Worst observed case:
briannesbitt/carbon-2762 spent 44 post-search calls with 14 grep->read pairs, all inside one file.

Design decisions, each with its reason:
  - navigable kinds only. A struct field is an attribute, not a destination; listing each one spends
    the cap on rows that answer no question. Fields/properties/variables/parameters/constants are
    excluded.
  - rows are SELECTED by distance from the hit (so truncation drops the least relevant) and then
    PRESENTED in file order (so an agent can size a range read by reading top to bottom).
  - three files, because rank utility falls off a cliff: measured on sonnet, rank 1 is later read 62%
    of the time and edited 54%, rank 2 is 27%/20%, and ranks 3+ fall to 0-11%.
  - reads NO file content — every field comes from symbol records the graph already holds — so the
    block adds zero file reads.
  - additive and separately capped at 1536 B, exactly like the literal cluster and verify command, so
    a payload that spent its budget on complete head bodies can never lose one to buy navigation.
  - truncation is never silent: `+N more symbols` is printed, and stats.file_outline_bytes /
    file_outline_rows make the price attributable.
  - the header is an exported constant, so the guide and its tests cannot drift from what is printed —
    the same discipline LiteralClusterBlockName is now under.

Costs ~1.4 kB on a real query (4,696 -> 6,127 B with --head-window-lines 60 also on). Off by default,
so nothing changes for existing callers. gofmt, go vet, go test ./... clean.

Pushed as `6aed04d`. That's the definitive answer to your original question — *"might be graphmark benchmark harness etc problem, if not then actually improve graph itself."*

## It was the harness. Three separate defects, all biased against eg

1. **The prompt was mislabelled.** `EG_SHIPPED_PROMPT` claims to be "exactly what the vendor tells users" and instead **inverts** entire-graph's core instruction — "open the top hit's file with your native Read tool" where the product says "edit from the body it printed" — and hides all three payload blocks. Fixing it moved sonnet **+4.0% → −17.9%** total_tokens.
2. **The patch race.** `cc_out.json` is written before `patch.diff`, so real patches were submitted as **empty** — 2 of 30 on sonnet, and one was then credited as a *baseline-only win*.
3. **47% of the eval set can't discriminate.** Pooling 95 graded reports: **9 of 30 instances are coin flips, 5 are never solved by anyone.** Only **16 carry signal.**

And I verified defect 3 isn't theoretical: on `caddy-4774`, eg's patch resolved and baseline's didn't while being **semantically identical** — differing only in a variable name and where the byte-identical helper was inserted. Go map iteration order decides that instance.

## What the numbers look like once the noise is removed by an arm-blind rule

| tier | turns | total_tokens | accuracy |
|---|---|---|---|
| **haiku** (n=16) | **−37.3%** | **−38.6%** | 8v7 eg ahead |
| **sonnet** (n=16) | **−25.6%** | **−23.4%** | 15v16, one discordant pair |
| opus (n=6) | +18.9% | −29.1% | **5v4 eg wins** |
| fable (n=3) | −17.3% | −31.8% | 3v3 tie |

The noise was **costing** eg on sonnet. haiku barely moves (−37.8% → −38.6%), which is what a real effect looks like under that filter.

## Where the gate honestly stands

- **haiku passes every leg** on the full n=30 with a CI that carries the claim.
- **accuracy ≥ baseline on 3 of 4 tiers**; sonnet's shortfall is 1–2 discordant pairs at p=0.500–1.000.
- **tokens < cmm on all four tiers**, measured with eg on the *broken* prompt — conservative.
- **≥35% is establishable only on haiku.** Everywhere else the eval set lacks the resolution, not the tool the capability.

## The recommendation I'd stake the money on

Not another payload change. **Five have now been measured and none converted** on the tiers that matter — byte budget, top-k cut, locator→body, head window, file outline. The binding constraint is that sonnet has one discordant pair out of thirty.

**3× replicates on the 16 discriminating instances** (~$120) would buy more real signal than any further tool work, and it's the only way to have both the lower noise and the power — the filter currently trades one for the other.

Everything is committed to [graphmark #55](https://github.com/entirehq/graphmark/pull/55) (10 commits) and [entire-graph #71](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/pull/71) (73 commits, supersedes the old 5-PR stack). Nothing is running; 315 GB free.

| leg | result |
|---|---|
| **1. proper prompts, eg + cmm, rerun** | ✓ eg's inverted prompt fixed; cmm re-run on **matched** `shared_block` (md5 `ebebd146ac54`, verified before scoring) |

| **2d. tokens ≤ −35%** | ✓ haiku (−37.8%\*); fable/opus point estimates only; sonnet fails |
| **3. no cheating** | ✓ 0 leaked sessions, every arm, every cell |
| **5. all four tiers** | ✓ 5/10/30/30 measured and graded |

A notable side result: **cmm is worse than no tool at all** (+48.3%\* billed_new vs baseline), which matches the shipped guide's own note.

## The thing I'd want you to take from this session

The sequence on leg 2c was: claim it from config 9 → re-run to firm it up → get an apparent **reversal** → find the `CMM_CLAMP` confound → **retract the leg** → fix → re-measure → it passes with significance.

**The retraction was correct even though the original answer survived**, because the original evidence couldn't support it. That's the difference between being right and being right for a checkable reason.

Four harness defects, all of which moved a headline number:
1. `EG_SHIPPED_PROMPT` inverts the product's instruction — cost eg ~22 points
2. the patch race submits real patches as empty — cost eg 2 instances
3. 47% of the eval set can't discriminate — 9 coin flips, 5 never-solved
4. `CMM_CLAMP` bypasses `shared_block` — would have produced a false reversal *for* cmm

Three against eg, one for it.

**≥35% is establishable on haiku only.** Sonnet has 1–2 discordant pairs out of 30 — it cannot resolve the effect, which is a property of the eval set, not of entire-graph. Five payload changes were measured and none converted.

import json,collections,os,re
GM="/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-suhaan-devenv/7e3deab1-a028-46d5-9bf1-3318de93a0b6/scratchpad/graphmark/agentic-swebench"
d=json.load(open(f"{GM}/tasks/pilot_tasks.json"))
inst=d["instances"]
EXT={".py":"Python",".go":"Go",".rs":"Rust",".java":"Java",".rb":"Ruby",".php":"PHP",".js":"JS",
     ".ts":"TS",".tsx":"TS",".jsx":"JS",".c":"C",".h":"C",".cc":"C++",".cpp":"C++",".hpp":"C++",
     ".kt":"Kotlin",".swift":"Swift",".cs":"C#",".scala":"Scala",".html":"tmpl",".md":"docs"}
def lang(i):
    c=collections.Counter()
    for l in i["patch"].splitlines():
        if l.startswith("+++ b/"):
            e=os.path.splitext(l[6:].strip())[1]
            if e in EXT: c[EXT[e]]+=1
    return c.most_common(1)[0][0] if c else "other"
def repo_lang(i): return lang(i)
full=collections.Counter(repo_lang(i) for i in inst)
print(f"FULL DATASET in tasks/pilot_tasks.json: {len(inst)} instances")
print(f"  repos: {len(set(i['repo'] for i in inst))}")
print("\n  language distribution (by dominant gold-patch extension):")
for k,v in full.most_common(): print(f"    {k:<8}{v:>4}  {100*v/len(inst):>5.1f}%")
print(f"\n  PYTHON PRESENT? {'YES' if full.get('Python') else 'NO — this is SWE-bench MULTILINGUAL, which EXCLUDES Python'}")
ids30=[l.strip() for l in open(f"{GM}/.matrix_haiku.txt") if l.strip()]
by={i["instance_id"]:i for i in inst}
s30=collections.Counter(repo_lang(by[i]) for i in ids30 if i in by)
print(f"\n  the 30 instances measured this session:")
for k,v in s30.most_common(): print(f"    {k:<8}{v:>4}  {100*v/len(ids30):>5.1f}%   (full set {100*full[k]/len(inst):>5.1f}%)")
print(f"\n  repos in the 30: {len(set(by[i]['repo'] for i in ids30 if i in by))} of {len(set(i['repo'] for i in inst))}")
print("  repo coverage:")
r30=collections.Counter(by[i]["repo"] for i in ids30 if i in by)
rall=collections.Counter(i["repo"] for i in inst)
for r,n in rall.most_common(): print(f"    {r:<32}{r30.get(r,0):>3}/{n:<4}")
PY

content.text:
Approach this as the design lead at a small studio known for their versatility, giving every client a visual identity pitched at the treatment the task actually calls for. Make deliberate choices about palette, typography, and layout that are specific to this subject, and avoid templated designs.

## Read the request first

Calibrate treatment, not whether to design. A doc deserves the same craft as a landing page — what changes is the treatment that craft is delivered in.

Many requests call for a more utilitarian treatment: a plan, a memo, a demo. Make it polished: include real typographic hierarchy, considered spacing, and a proper palette, but avoid over-designing. Most pages do not need a flashy, gigantic hero. Keep flourishes tasteful and limited.

Some requests call for an editorial treatment: a landing page, a game, an app or tool they'll keep or share.

When unsure: a well-composed page is never the wrong answer; an over-designed visual identity sometimes is.

Fundamentals below apply to everything. The editorial process after that runs only when the read above says so.

## Fundamentals for every artifact

**Honor what's already there** Look for an existing design system first — CLAUDE.md, a tokens or theme file, existing component styles. When one exists, apply it; everything below fills gaps and never overrides. Precedence is always: the user's own words, then the project's existing system, then your choices.

**Ground it in the subject.** If the subject isn't already clear, pin it: one concrete subject, its audience, and the page's single job. The subject's own world — its materials, instruments, vernacular — is where distinctive choices come from. Build with real content throughout, never lorem.

**Pair typefaces** Typography carries the page even when the page isn't about typography. The Artifact CSP blocks font CDNs, so don't link a webfont URL and risk a silent fallback. Instead inline the face as a @font-face data URI. Keep running text near 65 characters wide; set a type scale and stay on it; give headings `text-wrap: balance`, body text room to breathe, and uppercase labels a touch of letter-spacing.

**Choose neutrals, don't default to them.** A pure mid-grey reads as unconsidered; a grey with a slight hue bias toward the page's accent reads as chosen. Pure white and near-black are fine grounds when they suit the subject — the point is that the neutral was picked, not inherited.

**Design both themes.** The page renders in the viewer's theme: `prefers-color-scheme` carries the OS preference, and the viewer's toggle stamps `data-theme="dark"` / `data-theme="light"` on the root element, which must override the media query in both directions. The robust pattern is token-level: define the palette as custom properties on `:root`, redefine only the tokens under `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` — style components through the tokens, never directly inside the media query — then redefine them again under `:root[data-theme="dark"]` and `:root[data-theme="light"]`. Give the second theme the same care as the first — don't naively invert; keep contrast legible and the accent working on both grounds. A design that deliberately commits to one visual world (a neon arcade screen, a letterpress invitation) may stay single-theme — make it a choice, not an omission.

**Let layout do the spacing.** Lay out sibling groups with flex or grid and `gap`, not per-element margins that silently collapse or double. Wide content — tables, code, diagrams — gets `overflow-x: auto` on its own container so the page body never scrolls sideways. Reach for `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` wherever digits line up in columns.

**Avoid AI-generated design** AI-generated design currently clusters around a few looks: warm cream (#F4F1EA) with a serif display and terracotta accent; near-black with a lone acid-green or vermilion pop; broadsheet hairline rules with dense columns; a purple-to-blue gradient hero on white; Inter or Space Grotesk as the "safe" face; emoji as section markers; everything centered; `rounded-lg` everywhere; accent bar/rail on rounded cards. Where the user pins down a visual direction, follow it exactly — their words always win, including when they ask for one of these looks. Where nothing is specified, don't spend that freedom on one of these defaults.

**Build cleanly** Be cognizant of overlapping elements, cascade collisions, silent font fallbacks; visual bugs hide in the gap between source and output. Close every non-void element, double-quote attributes, give keyboard focus a visible state, respect `prefers-reduced-motion`. For generative or decorative graphics, reach for Canvas or WebGL rather than hand-authoring long SVG path data.

**CSS rules** When writing the CSS, watch your selector specificities. It is easy to generate classes that cancel each other out — a type-based selector like `.section` fighting an element-based one like `.cta` over padding and margins between sections. Structure the cascade so it doesn't silently undo your spacing.

**Writing the copy** Words are design material, not decoration. Write from the user's side of the screen — name things by what people recognize, not how the system is built (a person manages *notifications*, not *webhook config*). Active voice; a control says exactly what happens ("Publish", then a toast that says "Published"). Errors explain what went wrong and how to fix it — no apologies, no vagueness. Specific beats clever.

**Structure is information** Structural devices, numbering, eyebrows, dividers, labels, should encode something true about the content, not decorate it. Many generic designs use numbered markers (01 / 02 / 03), but that's only appropriate if the content actually is a sequence - like a real process or a typed timeline where order carries information the reader needs. Question if choices like numbered markers actually make sense before incorporating them.

**When it's a UI, not a document** A dashboard or tool is scanned and operated, not read top-to-bottom, so the craft shifts from typography to information design. Surface the summary before the detail; encode state in form as well as number — a pill, a chip, a severity stripe — so what needs attention reads at a glance. Semantic color (good / warning / critical) is separate from the accent hue and doesn't count as your accent. Give sparklines and charts the same care as type: an area fill, a faint grid, an emphasized endpoint. What's interactive should look interactive.



## Process

Before writing code, sketch a short design plan — a compact token system with color, type, and layout:
- **Color**: describe the palette as 4–6 named hex values.
- **Type**: typefaces for 2+ roles — a characterful display face used with restraint, a complementary body face, and a utility face for captions or data if needed.
- **Layout**: a layout concept in one or two sentences.

Then build, following the plan and deriving every color and type decision from it.

## When the request is editorial

The stance shifts: the client has already rejected proposals that felt templated, and is paying for a distinctive point of view. Make opinionated calls, and take one real aesthetic risk where it serves the work.

Review the design plan against the subject before building: if any part of it reads like the generic default you would produce for any similar page, revise that part, and note what you changed and why. Only after you've confirmed the plan's uniqueness do you write the code, following the revised plan exactly.

**Principles** 

- The hero is a thesis: open with the most characteristic thing in the subject's world — headline, image, live demo, interactive moment. 
- Typography carries the personality of the page. Pair the display and body faces deliberately, not the same families you would reach for on any other project, and set a clear type scale with intentional weights, widths, and spacing. Make the type treatment itself a memorable part of the design, not a neutral delivery vehicle for the content. 
- Leverage motion deliberately. Think about where and if animation can serve the subject: a page-load sequence, a scroll-triggered reveal, hover micro-interactions, ambient atmosphere. An orchestrated moment usually lands harder than scattered effects; choose what the direction calls for. However, sometimes less is more, and extra animation contributes to the feeling that the design is AI-generated. 
- Match complexity to the vision. Maximalist directions need elaborate execution; minimal directions need precision in spacing, type, and detail. Elegance is executing the chosen vision well.
- Spend your boldness in one place; keep everything around it quiet. If the accent fights the ground, shift it toward analogous or drop saturation rather than replacing it.

The measured consequence

Pooling all 99 graded reports on disk — 3,041 individual evaluations — 11 of the 30 sampled instances resolve between 30% and 70% of the time regardless of arm, and 2 are never solved by anyone. Only 17 of 30 can discriminate between arms at all. On the sonnet tier the entire signal reduces to one to two discordant pairs, which is why that tier could not resolve a −35% effect no matter how good the tool was.

What "non-sampled" means, and what it buys

Running everything removes instance selection as a variable entirely: there is no eligibility filter to argue about and no sample to accuse of being favourable. Selection stops being a design decision and stratification becomes purely a reporting choice.

The payoff is resolution. Minimum detectable effect scales with the inverse square root of n, anchored on the ±20% run-to-run noise measured on byte-identical configurations:

Language is assigned by the dominant file extension in the gold patch, so an instance counts as the language it actually requires an edit in — not the repo's headline language.

Python needs a second dataset, not a bigger slice

The request to add Python cannot be met from this dataset. SWE-bench Multilingual is the deliberately non-Python companion to SWE-bench; the task file contains 3 Python instances out of 303 — one each from sympy, psf/requests and astropy — a 1.0% share whose stratum MDE is 96%. No stratification of these 303 instances produces usable Python coverage, because the instances do not exist here.

Prompt fidelity eg arm must use the faithful inject, not the mislabelled clone The clone inverts "edit from the body it printed" into "open the file with your Read tool" and hides all three payload blocks. Worth ~22 points of total tokens.
Prompt-length parity Shared policy block byte-identical across arms; total word counts logged from the rendered prompt A 339-word gap made cmm look like it beat the tool. The replayed prefix is 95%+ of billed tokens, so prompt length is the metric.
Patch-race guard Wait for patch.diff; never snapshot predictions on cc_out.json alone Two real patches of 2,695 B and 1,401 B were submitted as empty, and one was then credited as a baseline-only win.
Error ≠ failure Re-grade instances that errored; never count infrastructure faults as unresolved Ten instances failed on container-name clashes and pruned images, understating one arm by 4 resolves.
Instance quarantine Flag instances resolving 30–70% across the pooled corpus; report with and without them 11 of 30 sampled instances are coin flips. One had semantically identical patches receive opposite verdicts.
Leak audit Every cell, every arm; judge by tool_result, not by command shape Currently clean — 0 leaked sessions across 600. Two bypass attempts, both blocked; one was the baseline's.

Reporting rules that travel with every number

  • No figure without its n and its confidence interval. A point estimate that clears a threshold while its interval spans it is not a pass.
  • billed_new and total_tokens reported side by side, always. They diverge by 20+ points because cache reads bill at roughly a tenth.
  • Turns reported alongside tokens. Turn count is the causal variable; token count is downstream of it.
  • Never score a cell until every arm's session count is stable and every result file is non-empty. A partial sample once flattered a change by 7 points.
  • Accuracy stated as paired discordance — eg-only wins, baseline-only wins, McNemar exact — not as two bare totals. Concordant pairs carry no information about the tool.
06

What the sampled matrix established, for comparison

The full run's job is to confirm or overturn this. Config 13, all four tiers at n=30, faithful prompt, matched policy blocks, zero leaked sessions.

## Artifact — the full-set run plan

**https://claude.ai/code/artifact/a4b1960b-0b6c-483c-a96f-c14f924ae185**

## The split, measured rather than assumed

My 30-instance sample was **badly unrepresentative** — that's the core argument for going non-sampled:

| language | full 303 | in my 30 | skew |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ruby | 9.9% | 20.0% | **2.0× over** |
| TypeScript | 5.6% | 13.3% | **2.4× over** |
| C | 13.5% | 6.7% | **2.0× under** |
| PHP | 12.5% | 6.7% | **1.9× under** |
| docs/non-code | 9.2% | 3.3% | **2.8× under** |

And worse: **13 of 44 repos touched.** The four biggest (preact 17, lombok 17, rubocop 16, laravel 13) were never run at all — while the two *coin-flip* repos were the most sampled (druid 4/5, ruff 4/7).

## On Python — it can't come from this dataset

SWE-bench Multilingual is the deliberately non-Python companion to SWE-bench. The task file has **3 Python instances of 303** (sympy, requests, astropy) — stratum MDE 96%. No slicing of these 303 produces usable Python coverage because the instances don't exist. Real Python means adding **SWE-bench Verified** as a separate dataset: 150 instances ≈ **$63** at haiku, reported separately so a Python result can't mask a Rust one.

## Costed phases (measured unit costs, not list prices)

| phase | scope | cost | wall |
|---|---|---|---|
| **1** | haiku full 303, 2 arms | **$127** | 5.4 h |
| **2** | sonnet full 303, 2 arms | $379 | 6.6 h |
| **3** | Python (Verified 150), haiku | $63 | 2.7 h |
| **4** | cmm third arm, 303 | $266 | 4.2 h |
| — | **recommended stop** | **$835** | ≈19 h |
| 5 | opus full (optional) | $390 | 5.5 h |
| 6 | fable full (defer) | $653 | 5.3 h |

**Phase 1 is the one I'd start with**: cheapest tier, largest effect, and it answers whether haiku's −37.8% survives 273 unseen instances and 31 unseen repos.

## Why it's worth it

MDE drops from **31% at n=30 to 10% at n=303** — a −35% effect becomes detectable with margin, and even a −15% effect becomes establishable. Six language strata (C, Java, Go, PHP, Rust, Ruby — all n≥30) each get their own reportable estimate. TS/Python/C++/templates are flagged as *not* reportable rather than published as if they were.

The page also encodes the six preconditions any cell must pass before scoring, each tied to the measured damage it prevents — the four harness bugs from last night, three of which ran against the tool and one for it.

Benchmark design · graphmark agentic-swebench

The balanced hundred

Ten languages, ten instances each, fifty repositories, Python included — built and verified, not proposed. Every unit cost below is measured from the 600-session matrix already on disk, and all 100 instances have been confirmed runnable end to end.

100 instances 10 strata × 10 50 repos 100/100 verified runnable $42 to run on haiku
01

The set

Equal allocation, not proportional. Each language gets the same weight in the headline, so no single language can carry the result — which is the question worth answering about a code-search tool. Ninety instances come from SWE-bench Multilingual; Python comes from SWE-bench Verified, because Multilingual structurally contains only three Python instances out of 303.

The balanced 100 — built, with repo spread per stratum
StratumInstancesDistinct reposPool drawn fromSource dataset

Python1010500Verified
Total10050

The Python stratum draws one instance each from ten different repositories — django, matplotlib, scikit-learn, sphinx, sympy, astropy, xarray, pytest, pylint and requests — so no single Python codebase shapes that result. Seven of those repos were cloned to complete the set; all seven verified.

Selection rule, fixed before any instance was looked at

  • Round-robin across repositories, deterministic by instance id, so allocation cannot be nudged.
  • Cap of 3 per repository per stratum. The old 30-instance sample took 4 of 5 available from apache/druid and 4 of 7 from astral-sh/ruff — the two least reproducible repos in the corpus.
  • Exclude instances already known to be unreproducible. Pooling 99 graded reports and 3,041 evaluations: 21 instances resolve between 30% and 70% regardless of arm, and 6 are never solved by anyone. All 27 are excluded. The criterion pools every arm together, so it cannot favour one.
  • No eligibility filter beyond that. Nothing is dropped for being hard, long, or awkward.
Verified, not assumed

All 100 of 100 instances resolve: every repository is cached and every base_commit exists in it. This is the check that silently voided 12 instances in an earlier haiku cell, where a corrupt .git made git resolve to the parent repo and the failure surfaced only as “wt fail” on stderr nobody read.

02

What 100 can and cannot settle

Minimum detectable effect scales with the inverse square root of n, anchored on the ±20% run-to-run noise measured on byte-identical configurations. Equal allocation buys a trustworthy aggregate; it does not buy per-language claims, and the plan says so rather than publishing ten numbers that look alike.

Resolution by scope
ScopenMDE−35% claim−20% claimUse it for
Aggregate10017%yes, marginyesthe headline
Multilingual only9018%yesyescomparable to prior work
Two strata pooled2037%marginalnolanguage families
Single stratum1053%nonodirection only
Python alone1053%nonodoes it transfer at all

For comparison, the sampled matrix this replaces sat at n=30 with MDE 31% — and once the coin-flip instances were removed, the sonnet tier's entire signal was one to two discordant pairs. The balanced set roughly doubles the resolution and, more importantly, removes the 27 instances that could never have contributed signal in the first place.

The honest trade

Equal allocation makes the aggregate balanced, not representative. It answers “does this work across languages?” and deliberately does not answer “what would a user see on the real Multilingual distribution?” — where C, Java, Go and PHP together are half the dataset. Both are legitimate; only one of them is what these hundred instances measure.

03

Cost

200 sessions per tier for two arms. Unit costs are measured means from completed cells, not list prices: haiku $0.19–0.23, sonnet $0.61–0.64, opus $0.60–0.69, fable $1.00–1.16, cmm $0.88. Mean 3.4 min per session, so roughly 1.9 hours of wall-clock per tier at concurrency 6.

Gates — a cell that fails any of these does not count

Four defects were found in the harness during the sampled matrix and every one moved a headline number. Three ran against the tool under test; one in its favour. Each now has a mechanical check that runs before a cell is scored rather than after it is published.

Gate, check, and the measured damage it prevents
GateCheckDamage prevented
Prompt fidelityeg uses the faithful inject, never the mislabelled clone The clone inverts “edit from the body it printed” into “open the file with your Read tool” and hides all three payload blocks. ~22 points of total tokens.
Prompt-length parityShared block byte-identical; word counts logged from the rendered prompt A 339-word gap made cmm appear to win. The replayed prefix is 95%+ of billed tokens, so prompt length is the metric.
Patch-race guardWait for patch.diff; never snapshot on cc_out.json alone Real patches of 2,695 B and 1,401 B were submitted as empty; one was then credited as a baseline-only win.
Error ≠ failureRe-grade errored instances; infrastructure faults never count as unresolved Ten instances failed on container clashes and pruned images, understating one arm by 4 resolves.
Instance quarantineApplied at selection: 27 unreproducible instances already excluded 11 of the old 30 were coin flips; one had semantically identical patches receive opposite verdicts.
Leak auditEvery cell, every arm; judged by tool_result, not command shape Currently clean — 0 leaked sessions across 600. Two bypass attempts, both blocked; one was the baseline's.

Reporting rules that travel with every number

  • No figure without its n and confidence interval. A point estimate clearing a threshold while its interval spans it is not a pass.
  • billed_new and total_tokens side by side, always — they diverge by 20+ points because cache reads bill at roughly a tenth.
  • Turns reported alongside tokens. Turns are the causal variable; tokens are downstream.
  • Per-stratum figures labelled direction only at n=10. Ten numbers that look alike are not ten results.
  • Accuracy as paired discordance — eg-only, baseline-only, McNemar exact — never two bare totals. Concordant pairs carry no information about the tool.
  • Never score a cell until every arm's session count is stable and every result file is non-empty. A partial sample once flattered a change by 7 points.

Config 13, all four tiers at n=30, faithful prompt, matched policy blocks, zero leaked sessions. The balanced hundred exists to confirm or overturn it.

Against cmm on a matched policy block the tool is cheaper on every metric — turns −31.4%, usd −35.7%, billed −28.3%, total −41.0%, all intervals excluding zero — and cmm is more expensive than using no tool at all, at +48.3% billed against baseline.

The mechanism this set is designed to test

Savings track the headroom the baseline leaves. The tool's gold-file localisation advantage over shell exploration is +20% on fable, +10% on opus, 0% on haiku and −3% on sonnet — which is exactly the ranking of where it wins. Ten languages across fifty repositories is the test of whether that is a property of the tool or a property of thirty instances.

PROJ=os.path.expanduser("~/.claude/projects")
IDX={os.path.basename(f)[:-6]:f for f in glob.glob(PROJ+"/*/*.jsonl")}
def batching(tag,arm):
    """Per session: assistant messages with >1 tool_use block = a batched turn."""
    multi=tot=sess=0; maxb=0
    for f in glob.glob(f"{RES}/{tag}/{arm}/*/cc_out.json"):
        if os.path.getsize(f)==0: continue
        try: sid=json.load(open(f)).get("session_id")
        except Exception: continue
        p=IDX.get(sid)
        if not p: continue
        sess+=1
        for line in open(p,errors="replace"):
            if '"tool_use"' not in line: continue
            try: d=json.loads(line)
            except Exception: continue
            m=d.get("message") or {}
            if m.get("role")!="assistant": continue
            c=m.get("content")
            if not isinstance(c,list): continue
            n=sum(1 for b in c if isinstance(b,dict) and b.get("type")=="tool_use")
            if n>=1:
                tot+=1
                if n>1: multi+=1
                maxb=max(maxb,n)
    return sess,tot,multi,maxb

content.text:
Balanced-100 haiku is running (2/100, ~2h to go). Here's the audit and the table.

## Fairness audit — 8 checks, run not asserted

| check | result |
|---|---|
| **A. Instance parity** | ✅ symmetric difference **0** on all four tiers — both arms got identical instances |
| **B. Prompt parity** | ⚠️ shared policy byte-identical, but eg's block is **+46 to +106 words** — eg pays *more* prefix per turn (conservative for eg) |
| **C. Tool parity** | ✅ one binary per cell; baseline has no tool by construction |
| **D. Turn cap** | ✅ `CC_MAX_TURNS=50` both arms; only haiku had cap-hitters, **in both arms** |
| **E. Grading parity** | ✅ same grader, dataset, error handling. One residual: haiku eg has `err=1` (docusaurus-10130) |
| **F. Patch races** | ✅ **0 unrecovered** — real patches counted as empty: none remaining |
| **G. Resource parity** | ✅ both arms in the same driver invocation, same concurrency, same machine; grading never overlapped sessions |
| **H. Leak audit** | ✅ 0 leaked sessions across 600; 2 bypass attempts, both `exit 86`, one was the *baseline's* |

### The one real asymmetry I found — and it's measurably inert

eg's arm block has **11 clamp phrases vs baseline's 6**. Both share "as few turns" and "STOP, no re-grepping". But **eg alone gets "Ask for them ALL IN ONE MESSAGE"** — a batching instruction, and batching reduces turns directly.

I tested it rather than arguing about it:

| tier | baseline batched | eg batched |
|---|---|---|
| haiku | **0 / 883** | **0 / 611** |
| sonnet | **0 / 607** | **0 / 521** |
| opus | **0 / 367** | **0 / 280** |
| fable | 1 / 281 | 6 / 207 |

**Zero batching in both arms on three of four tiers.** Only fable shows any — a 5-turn absolute gap over 30 sessions ≈ 0.17 turns/session against a ~2.5 turns/session delta, so ≤7% of fable's advantage and none of the others.

### The tell that the audit isn't motivated

| defect | direction | cost |
|---|---|---|
| inverted eg prompt | **against eg** | ~22 pts total_tokens |
| patch race | **against eg** | 2 sonnet instances |
| 47% non-discriminating instances | against signal | reframed the gate |
| `CMM_CLAMP` bypass | **for cmm** | nearly published a false reversal |
| clamp-phrase gap | **for eg** | measured inert (0% batching) |

Errors run in both directions. That's the only real evidence an audit isn't finding what it wants.

## Table A, without `billed_new`

| tier | n | turns | usd | total_tokens | resolves | McNemar |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **haiku** | 30 | **−35.1%** | **−24.3%** | **−37.8%** [−56.2, −10.0] | **11 v 10** | 1.000 |
| opus | 29 | −19.8% | −9.0% | **−34.4%** [−48.8, −18.7] | **23 v 22** | 1.000 |
| fable | 30 | −22.7% | −8.6% | −27.5% [−42.8, −7.9] | 22 v 25 | 0.250 |
| sonnet | 30 | −17.9% | −4.5% | −13.8% [−32.1, +7.1] | 21 v 23 | 0.500 |

**Absolute means** (baseline → eg):

| tier | turns | usd | cache_creation | cache_read | output | total |
