1	# entire-graph on Sonnet: accuracy + token-savings findings
2	
3	**Author:** live hands-on test by Sonnet 5, 2026-08-01, inside `devenv/` (cli, entiredb,
4	entire-api, entire.io). Not a benchmark run — no Docker grading, no synthetic SWE-bench
5	harness. Every number below is a command I actually ran and an output I actually read,
6	plus one real historical query against 27 of my own past sessions in this project. Where
7	a claim is modeled/estimated rather than measured, it says so.
8	
9	This complements — and root-causes — the standing statistical research already on file
10	(`graph-swebench-verdict`, `sonnet-band-structure`, `verify-block-is-the-lever`,
11	`eg-usage-is-invariant`, `eg-ab-testing-cache-trap`). That work measured *that* Sonnet's
12	graph usage is flat and the token effect is near-zero to negative. This is *why*.
13	
14	---
15	
16	## TL;DR
17	
18	- **Retrieval accuracy is genuinely good on clean input: 6/7 real tasks nailed the correct
19	  hit.** The 7th failed for a specific, reproducible reason (below), not because ranking is
20	  bad in general.
21	- **When a graph call actually resolves and chains correctly, the token ratio is real and
22	  large — ~23x measured on one real case** (4,578 bytes returned vs 106,707 bytes of
23	  counterfactual whole-file reads).
24	- **None of that shows up in aggregate** because, across 27 real sessions in this exact
25	  project, I invoke the graph as the *first* locate action **0% of the time**, and locate
26	  calls are outnumbered by grep/read exploration **627 to 1**. Estimated savings are 0.23%
27	  of total session tokens.
28	- I found **five concrete, reproducible mechanical bugs** that explain that gap. The
29	  headline one — `.entire/metadata/` (178–198 MB of gitignored session transcripts per
30	  repo) gets indexed and can outrank real source code in search results — is new and not
31	  in any prior write-up.
32	
33	---
34	
35	## Part 1 — Accuracy
36	
37	Methodology: pick a real symbol/behavior I didn't already have open, write a natural-language
38	query for it (not the function name), run `entire graph search --profile full|fast`, judge
39	the top hit against the actual file.
40	
41	| # | Repo (lang) | Query | Result |
42	|---|---|---|---|
43	| 1 | cli (Go) | "OPF pre-push redaction rewrites unpushed v1 checkpoint commits before push" | ✅ rank 1 = `ManualCommitStrategy.prePush`, complete function body, correct |
44	| 2 | entiredb (Go) | "atomic repair of under-replicated repos in the DHT repair queue" | ✅ rank 1 = `RepairQueue.scanUnderReplicated`, complete body + covering test + declarations |
45	| 3 | entire-api (Go) | "usage cap park and replay for checkpoint analysis Anthropic calls" | ✅ rank 1 = `checkpointAnalysis`, rank 2 = `ReplayDeferredAnalysis` — both real and relevant |
46	| 4 | entire.io (TS) | "resolve externalized image placeholders in transcript to real assets from R2" | ✅ rank 1 = `resolveImagePlaceholders`, complete body + call-site comment + declarations |
47	| 5 | entiredb (Go) | ambiguous symbol `Close` (54 matches, deliberately generic) | ✅ correctly refused to guess — printed all 54 with copy-pasteable `--symbol/--file/--line` selectors |
48	| 6 | entiredb (Go) | `entire graph diff --base 743d99c29 --head HEAD -- dht/repair_queue.go` | ✅ accurate entity-level diff: field rename (`convergeAnchor`→`convergeTicks`) + 7 changed method bodies, matching the real commit messages exactly, in **1.2s** |
49	| 7 | entire-api (Go) | "verify a cell request bearer JWT against entire-core JWKS" | ❌ rank 1 and rank 2 were **not code** — they were quotes from old Claude Code session transcripts under `.entire/metadata/`, outranking the real answer (`Authenticator.verifyBearer`), which was pushed to rank 3 |
50	
51	**6 of 7 clean. The one miss is the important finding — not noise, a real bug:**
52	
53	### The `.entire/metadata` bug
54	
55	`entire-api/.entire/.gitignore` explicitly ignores `metadata/`. It is not tracked by git
56	(`git ls-files` returns nothing). It is nonetheless walked and indexed by
57	`entire graph search`, and it is **178–198 MB per repo across all four repos I checked**:
58	
59	```
60	cli         184M
61	entiredb    182M
62	entire-api  198M
63	entire.io   178M
64	```
65	
66	Contents are literal past Claude Code session transcripts (`file-history-snapshot`, the
67	same JSONL format this very session is being written to). One file I checked
68	(`entire-api/.entire/metadata/de272.../full.jsonl`) is **191.6 MB by itself**, and it
69	happened to contain a prior session where I (a past instance of me) had already debugged
70	this exact JWT/JWKS question and pasted the real source into my own final answer. That
71	pasted quote — not the code itself — is what won rank 1 and rank 2.
72	
73	This is a **self-reinforcing trust-degradation loop**: the more times a symbol gets
74	discussed in a Claude Code session (which Entire's own checkpoint capture writes to
75	`.entire/metadata`), the more that transcript noise competes with, and can outrank, the
76	actual source for that exact symbol in future graph searches. Popular / frequently-debugged
77	code is *specifically* the code most at risk of this.
78	
79	**Confirmed fix:** passing `--ignore-file` with `.entire/metadata/` excluded restores the
80	correct ranking (`Authenticator.verifyBearer` at rank 2, no transcript noise) — see Part 3,
81	bug 1, for the full repro and a second effect this fix has on latency.
82	
83	**Why this matters for "not trusting it":** doctrine rule 3 says *"a `complete-symbol` hit
84	is the whole function: edit it"* — i.e., trust rank 1 blindly. On this query, rank 1 was a
85	203-character JSON-escaped fragment of a chat transcript. An agent following the doctrine
86	literally would have tried to edit a log file.
87	
88	---
89	
90	## Part 2 — Token savings
91	
92	### 2a. Real historical numbers (27 of my actual sessions in this project, all-time)
93	
94	From `entire graph stats --repo . --since all` (measured, not modeled):
95	
96	```
97	graph calls (all verbs):        168   →  only 79 are locate calls (search/impact/neighbors)
98	exploration calls:            49,548   (35,390 Bash grep/find/cat · 7,217 whole-file reads · 6,940 line-range reads)
99	sessions that needed to locate:    8 (of 27)
100	graph-first rate:                 0%   — never once the first locate action
101	estimated savings:            31.6M tokens  =  0.23% of total session tokens (~4.9% of non-cache-read tokens)
102	```
103	
104	The estimator here is deliberately conservative (credits one locate call with one whole-file
105	read it replaced) and is explicitly described by the tool itself as an underestimate of real
106	baseline behavior. Even so: **0.23% is not "the tool doesn't save tokens" — it's "the tool is
107	almost never invoked."**
108	
109	### 2b. Real measured per-task ratio (not modeled — actual bytes, one real case)
110	
111	Task 2 from Part 1 (`RepairQueue.scanUnderReplicated`, entiredb), captured with `wc -c` on
112	the actual command output and the actual files involved:
113	
114	```
115	entire graph search (fast profile):     2,915 bytes  (≈  729 tokens)
116	entire graph impact (fast profile):     1,663 bytes  (≈  416 tokens)
117	                                    -----------------
118	combined graph payload:                 4,578 bytes  (≈ 1,145 tokens)
119	
120	counterfactual — whole-file reads of the 3 files this task actually touches:
121	  dht/repair_queue.go            48,811 bytes
122	  dht/repair_queue_test.go       46,245 bytes
123	  dht/provider.go                11,651 bytes
124	                                -----------------
125	  total                         106,707 bytes  (≈ 26,677 tokens)
126	
127	ratio: ~23x fewer tokens, when the chain resolves cleanly.
128	```
129	
130	This is the number that should scale — and does not, because of what's in Part 3.
131	
132	### 2c. Why 2a and 2b don't reconcile
133	
134	The per-call ratio (2b) is real. The aggregate (2a) is near-zero. The gap is fully
135	accounted for by mechanics, not by retrieval quality:
136	
137	- **Latency tax discourages chaining.** Every `search`/`impact`/`neighbors` call against
138	  entiredb cost 55–60s (`--profile full`) or ~16s (`--profile fast`) to cold-index — even
139	  back-to-back, even with an explicit `--cache-dir`. Getting the 23x ratio in 2b required
140	  *two* successful calls plus one that failed outright (see bug 2 below); that's 2-3
141	  minutes of wall-clock for a task an agent optimizing for turn latency will often just
142	  grep instead.
143	- **The natural chain breaks on first use** (bug 3). `search` reports one line number for a
144	  symbol; `impact --symbol file:line` needs a different one for the same symbol. The
145	  doctrine's own worked example ("search once, then chain into impact") fails the first
146	  time an agent tries it literally.
147	- **The documented recovery path for a failed build doesn't exist** (bug 4) — so even the
148	  one place token savings should be uncontroversial (verify-once instead of a grep-hunting
149	  loop) is a dead end.
150	- **A second, competing doctrine is loaded every session** (bug 5) and points at a thinner
151	  tool first.
152	
153	---
154	
155	## Part 3 — Mechanical bugs (all reproduced live in this session)
156	
157	### Bug 1 — `.entire/metadata/` pollutes search ranking (and, in some repos, latency)
158	
159	Repro:
160	```
161	cd entire-api
162	entire graph search --repo . --profile fast \
163	  --query "verify a cell request bearer JWT against entire-core JWKS" --top-k 5
164	# rank 1, rank 2 = .entire/metadata/<session>/full.jsonl (chat transcript), real answer at rank 3
165	
166	echo '.entire/metadata/' > ignore.txt
167	entire graph search --repo . --profile fast --ignore-file ignore.txt \
168	  --query "verify a cell request bearer JWT against entire-core JWKS" --top-k 5
169	# rank 2 = Authenticator.verifyBearer (correct), no transcript noise
170	# ALSO: 24.68s -> 1.73s wall time for the identical query
171	```
172	Confirmed the size/tracked-status claim independently:
173	```
174	git check-ignore -v .entire/metadata     # -> .entire/.gitignore:3:metadata/  (it IS gitignored)
175	git ls-files .entire/metadata            # -> empty (it is NOT tracked)
176	du -sh .entire/metadata                  # -> 198M
177	```
178	Repeated the size check on all four repos: 184M / 182M / 198M / 178M. All four are exposed.
179	
180	The latency win from excluding it did **not** reproduce on entiredb (stayed ~16s on fast
181	profile with or without the ignore file) — entiredb's genuine source tree (2,540 files) is
182	apparently large enough that metadata isn't the dominant cost there. So: confirmed fix for
183	ranking pollution in all repos; latency benefit is repo-dependent, not universal.
184	
185	**Fix:** the indexer should honor `.gitignore` by default, or hard-exclude `.entire/metadata`
186	specifically — it is Entire's own product data, not user code, in every repo that has ever
187	used Entire.
188	
189	### Bug 2 — `impact --symbol <file>:<line>` rejects the line `search` just reported
190	
191	```
192	entire graph search ... → dht/repair_queue.go:676-744  symbol=RepairQueue.scanUnderReplicated
193	entire graph impact --repo . --symbol dht/repair_queue.go:676
194	# -> "No symbols matched ... at line 676" (after paying the full 58s cold-index cost)
195	
196	entire graph impact --repo . --symbol "RepairQueue.scanUnderReplicated"
197	# -> works; resolves to dht/repair_queue.go:684 (the func line, 8 lines after the snippet start)
198	```
199	`search`'s reported snippet start includes leading comment lines; `impact`'s file:line
200	selector needs the exact declaration line. The two verbs disagree about what "this
201	symbol's line" means for the same symbol.
202	
203	**Fix:** `impact`/`neighbors` should snap a `file:line` selector to the nearest enclosing
204	definition, the way an IDE "go to definition" does, instead of requiring an exact match.
205	
206	### Bug 3 — index never warm-cached in this session, even with explicit `--cache-dir`
207	
208	```
209	entire graph impact --repo . --symbol "RepairQueue.scanUnderReplicated" --format json --cache-dir "$CD"
210	# index_cache_hit:false, index_latency_ms: 58520
211	
212	entire graph impact --repo . --symbol "RepairQueue.scanUnderReplicated" --format json --cache-dir "$CD"
213	# (identical call, same dir, immediately after) index_cache_hit:false, index_latency_ms: 55746
214	```
215	Same result at `--profile fast` (two back-to-back calls, both `index_cache_hit:false`,
216	~16s each). This directly extends the previously-known `eg-ab-testing-cache-trap` finding
217	(cache is tree-keyed, not binary-keyed) — here it's not keyed wrong, it plain isn't hitting.
218	
219	**Fix:** verify `--cache-dir` persistence works at all in the currently-distributed build;
220	if it does elsewhere, something in this environment (three different binaries on PATH,
221	below) is bypassing it.
222	
223	### Bug 4 — `entire graph explain` (doctrine hard rule 6d) does not exist
224	
225	`.entire/graph-agent.md`, in bold, calls this a hard rule where "each violation costs real
226	money": pipe a failed build through `entire graph explain --repo .`. Live repro:
227	```
228	# introduced a real compile error (perf.Start -> perf.StartX) in an isolated worktree
229	go build ./cmd/entire/cli/strategy/... 2>&1 | entire graph explain --repo .
230	# -> unknown command "explain"
231	```
232	Checked every graph binary on PATH:
233	```
234	~/.local/share/entire/plugins/bin/entire-graph        --help | grep -i explain   # (nothing)
235	~/.local/share/entire/plugins/bin/entire-graph-fresh   --help | grep -i explain   # (nothing)
236	~/.local/share/entire/plugins/bin/entire-graph-mainrel                            # dangling symlink into a wiped /tmp path
237	```
238	None have it. This is the doctrine's own designated "don't grep, verify properly" step,
239	and it fails on the very first try, for every agent, every time.
240	
241	**Fix:** implement `explain`, or strip rule 6d from `graph-agent.md` until it's real —
242	right now it actively trains an agent to distrust the rest of the doctrine.
243	
244	### Bug 5 — two competing tool doctrines load in the same session
245	
246	- Global `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`: *"prefer one brain/graph call... `entire sem edges|symbols
247	  --repo . --format ndjson`, `entire sem diff`..."*
248	- Project `devenv/CLAUDE.md` → `.entire/graph-agent.md`: `entire graph search/impact/
249	  neighbors/explain`
250	
251	`entire sem --help` confirms it's a distinct, older binary with no `search`, `impact`, or
252	`neighbors` — only `commit/checkpoint/diff/analyze/doctor/version/capabilities/snapshot/
253	symbols/edges`. An agent that follows the *global* instruction first (it's the one that
254	says "always") hits a capability ceiling before it ever reaches the richer tool the
255	*project* instruction recommends.
256	
257	**Fix:** reconcile the two — either retire `entire sem` guidance globally, or make it
258	explicit that `entire graph` supersedes it and should be preferred whenever a project has
259	`.entire/graph-agent.md` installed.
260	
261	---
262	
263	## Part 4 — Recommendations, in order of leverage
264	
265	1. **Exclude `.entire/metadata/` from the index by default** (bug 1). Highest leverage:
266	   fixes a real accuracy bug present in 100% of repos checked, and cuts latency
267	   dramatically in at least one of four.
268	2. **Fix or remove `entire graph explain`** (bug 4). A hard rule that fails on first use is
269	   worse than no rule.
270	3. **Fix `--cache-dir` reuse** (bug 3). Turns every second-and-later graph call in a session
271	   from ~15–60s to near-zero — this is very likely the single biggest lever on whether an
272	   agent chains 2–3 graph calls (as the doctrine wants) versus bailing to grep after one.
273	4. **Make `impact`/`neighbors --symbol file:line` snap to the enclosing definition** (bug 2)
274	   so `search → impact` actually chains as documented.
275	5. **Reconcile the global `entire sem` doctrine with the project `entire graph` doctrine**
276	   (bug 5) so there's one recommended tool, not two.
277	
278	None of these require improving retrieval quality — that part already works (6/7, and the
279	7th was an indexing-scope bug, not a ranking bug). All five are about removing friction
280	between a correct answer and an agent actually receiving and trusting it.

# Sonnet: fix the 11 repos that lose, by killing post-edit churn

## Context

On rep30/Sonnet the tool now scores **−2.7% pooled** (two runs of the v13 confidence tier, n=30
instances / 59 runs), up from +9.4%. That average hides a clean bimodal split, and the split — not
the average — is the thing to fix:

| group | n | cost | baseline turns → eg turns |
|---|---|---|---|
| turn-COLLAPSE (winners) | 15 | **−31.9%** | 24.7 → 19.1 |
| turn-EXPLOSION (losers) | 11 | **+52.1%** | 16.4 → 25.6 |
| other losers (flat) | 4 | +8.8% | ~unchanged |

Same tool, same config, same prompt: on 15 repos it roughly halves the session and on 11 it nearly
doubles it. **The winning mechanism already exists** — the plan is to find why 11 repos invert it.

### Why this is worth doing: the arithmetic

| if the 11 explosion repos reached… | suite |
|---|---|
| parity with baseline (0%) | −16.5% |
| −15% | −21.4% |
| −30%, i.e. what the 15 winners already get | **−26.8%** |
| (every loser at parity, explosion included) | −17.5% |

So the 25% goal is reachable **only** through this group, and only if they behave like the winners
rather than merely stop losing. Nothing else on the board moves the number.

### The target set (11 instances, 8 languages)

`gson-2479` +107% · `laravel-48636` +104% · `hugo-12562` +78% · `gson-2158` +72% ·
`vuejs-11870` +60% · `scikit-learn-14629` +57% · `fmt-2457` +47% · `lombok-3486` +31% ·
`ruff-15626` +30% · `immutable-js-2006` +21% · `lucene-13170` +2%

## The mechanism, measured

Deltas are eg minus its OWN paired baseline, so task difficulty is already differenced out.

| per-session delta | EXPLOSION (n=10) | COLLAPSE (n=7) |
|---|---|---|
| **calls AFTER the first edit** | **+7.95** | **−5.64** |
| throwaway repro commands | +1.10 | −4.93 |
| build/test calls | +1.50 | +0.14 |
| edit calls | +1.05 | −1.57 |
| distinct files edited | +0.10 | −1.36 |

**The entire difference is post-edit.** Both groups reach a first edit fine — the payload does its
job. Then the explosion group enters a verify → repro → re-edit loop and the collapse group stops.
A 13.6-call swing on the post-edit phase alone.

### What has already been ruled out as the trigger

- **Payload block presence.** Fires at the same rate in both groups, and the explosion group gets
  *more*: VERIFY 80% vs 71%, COVERING TEST 30% vs 14%, RELATED SITES 90% vs 93%, SAME-CONCEPT 85%
  vs 79%. Content is not the discriminator.
- **Retrieval quality.** gold@1 `gson-2479` = +107%; gold@1 `faker-2970` = −49%; gold MISSED
  `phpspreadsheet-4214` = −52%. Gold rank does not separate the groups.
- **Language.** The 11 span C++, Go, Java, JavaScript, PHP, Python, Rust, TypeScript.
- **Payload width.** Measured U-curve: 12 bodies +18.9%, 5 bodies +9.4%, 3 bodies −2.7%, 0 bodies
  (locators only) +1.9%. The optimum is already at 3; both directions are worse.
- Ten mechanisms refuted with symmetric prompts: dispersion gating, VERIFY-target binding,
  build-check coverage, query-declaration block, the `def` prompt line (3×), literal-occurrence
  block, 1-hop callees, escalation-on-demand, uniform widening, locations-only.

## The work

### 1. Identify the post-edit trigger — this gates everything else

An Explore agent is building a turn-by-turn trace of all 16 instances (11 explosion + 5 collapse
controls), locating the divergence turn in each and testing: edit churn, verification churn, repro
scaffolding, payload misdirection, post-edit re-searching. `phpspreadsheet-4214` is the control that
kills a bad theory — gold MISSED and it still wins −52%.

Do not proceed to §2 until this names a trigger that is present in ≥7 of the 11 and absent in the
collapse group. If no such trigger exists, say so and stop: the split would then be task-intrinsic
and not addressable from the tool.

### 2. Intervene on the trigger, tool-side only

The change must be in what `search` RETURNS. Prompt text is excluded — measured three times not to
be a lever, and the one attempt (naming `def`) moved a cell from −0.6% to +14.9%.

Two candidates the data already points at, to be confirmed or discarded by §1:

- **The post-edit phase has no payload at all.** Everything is delivered at turn 1 and the churn
  happens 10+ turns later. Zero-toll re-delivery already exists and is unbenchmarked
  (`ENTIRE_GRAPH_PRESEARCH`, on `test/all-agent-fixes`); it would let the covering test and related
  sites be re-presented at edit time without costing a message.
- **Repro scaffolding is 6 calls of the swing.** COVERING TEST names the existing test and fires on
  only 30% of the explosion group. Raising its hit rate is a bounded, testable change — but note it
  fires *more* there than in the collapse group, so this is a hypothesis, not a conclusion.

### 3. Verify — the gates that have caught three bad changes this session

1. **Free offline replay first.** Re-issue the recorded queries in `results/R30Sv13/eg/*/gq_calls.log`
   against `replay-wt/<iid>` with a **separate `--cache-dir` per binary** (the index cache is
   tree-keyed, not binary-keyed — reuse one dir and the second build silently returns the first's
   payloads). Assert gold rank does not regress on any of the 30.
2. **Mutation-verify every regression test**: confirm it fails with the change reverted. A test that
   passes either way is worthless — this caught a bad VERIFY fix earlier today.
3. **Haiku do-no-harm.** Haiku is the one model where the tool works (−25.0% CI [−32.2, −17.0]).
   Any change ships only if a paired Haiku cell stays within noise of that. The tier passed this
   (+0.7%, CI [−17.2, +23.7]); the next change must too.
4. **Pre-register before spending**, in the style of `PREDICTION-v13b.md`: state the target metric,
   the pass/fail bound, and what will be withdrawn if it fails. The exploration-heavy subgroup was
   read post-hoc once and had to be withdrawn when the replicate came in at −15.8% against run 1's
   −23.4%.
5. **Replicate the winning config**, do not compare it to a different config. Two runs of v13 differ
   by 7.6 points on the same instances; a single cell cannot resolve anything smaller.

## Files

- `eg-consolidated/internal/sem/search.go`, `internal/cli/search.go` — payload assembly and the text
  renderer (`writeTextSearchResult`, `searchTextFullRanks`)
- `eg-consolidated/internal/sem/search_covertest.go` — COVERING TEST selection, if §1 implicates it
- `graphmark-bench/agentic-swebench/tools/_egsearch.py` — the tier lives here; `EG_CONF_TIER`,
  `EG_CONF_NARROW`. **Trap:** `tools/eg-q`'s `_pp()` only runs this filter for a whitelist of env
  flags, and `run_3arm.sh` must pass any new var through — miss either and the cell measures nothing
  while appearing to run.
- **Do not touch** the prompt blocks in `run_3arm.sh`.

## Honest expectation

Reaching −26.8% requires an 82-point swing on 11 instances (+52.1% → −30%). Nothing measured this
session has moved a group that far. Parity (−16.5% suite) is the realistic target and would still be
the best Sonnet result by a wide margin. I will report the interval and say plainly if the 25% goal
is not met rather than reframing the claim — and if §1 finds no addressable trigger, the correct
outcome is to stop, not to try an eleventh mechanism.

5. **Replicate the winning config**, do not compare it to a different config. Two runs of v13 differ

§1 is answered decisively. **The trigger is the post-*last*-edit verification tail — AUC 0.945.**

```
calls after FINAL edit    baseline -> eg      delta
EXPLOSION (n=11)          4.18 -> 10.05       +5.86
COLLAPSE  (n=5)           5.40 ->  3.40       -2.00
                                              gap +7.86  (63% of the total)
```

And **every explosion tail is toolchain repair, never code work**:
```
composer install · pnpm install --frozen-lockfile ×2 · find / -iname "*cmdreader*"
find ~/.m2 -iname "error_prone_annotations*.jar" · find / -maxdepth 6 -iname "site-packages"
```

**The control that isolates it is `phpspreadsheet`.** It has *exactly* laravel's environment defect — no `vendor/`, phpunit unavailable, `composer install` blocked. laravel **+10.5 turns**, phpspreadsheet **−14.5**. The difference is what the payload named:

- **laravel** → source symbols only. The agent found the test class itself and tried to **execute** it → composer/phpunit chase.
- **phpspreadsheet** → `tests/data/Calculation/MathTrig/ROUNDDOWN.php`, a **table of expected values**. The agent `cat`-ed it at call #4 and never booted phpunit. Gold was *missed* and it still won −52%.

And `fluentd` is the mirror image, proving it from the other side: it wins **on the tail** (11 calls → 2) purely because VERIFY named the correct test path, deleting an 11-call filename hunt.

**So the lever is not whether VERIFY exists — I measured that as no-signal — it's whether the oracle is *readable* or *runnable*.** Six of eight eg runs that executed the literal VERIFY line errored.

This also kills three of my own standing theories: gold-miss recovery costs ~0 (all three misses were recovered in 1–2 greps), repro scaffolding was an artifact of two baseline outliers, and payload misdirection is dead (the collapse group edits the top hit *less* often).

A second, independent finding worth recording: **eg has a hard localization floor.** Its first edit lands at call ~10.05 regardless of difficulty, while the baseline's varies from 8.18 (easy) to 22.0 (hard). That's why it wins where baseline localization is slow and loses where it's already fast — `corr(baseline first-edit index, Δturns) = −0.665`.

I'm at the edge of my context, so rather than start an implementation I'd have to abandon mid-way, here's the precise handoff — §2 of the approved plan, now with the trigger named:

**Highest-value change, with its proof:** in `internal/sem/search_verify.go`, prefer a **read-oracle** over a run-oracle. Where an expected-value fixture or table-driven data file exists for the subject, inline it and suppress the executable VERIFY. Where no runnable command exists, say so explicitly rather than emitting one that errors. phpspreadsheet is the existence proof that this alone flips a broken-harness instance from +10 turns to −14.

The plan file already carries the verification gates (offline replay with separate cache dirs, mutation-verified tests, Haiku do-no-harm, pre-registration, replicate-don't-compare).

**Implemented and mutation-verified.** The read-oracle change is in `internal/sem/search_verify.go`, full `internal/sem` suite green, and the regression test **fails with the change reverted** — so it's testing the behaviour, not passing vacuously.

What it does: when the derived VERIFY command's runner isn't installed, the block stops handing the agent a command it will run and fail, and instead names the same file to **read**:

```
VERIFY BY READING: internal/a/a_test.go
  This checkout cannot run `go test ./internal/a -run '^TestDispatch$'` (its runner is
  not installed), so do NOT try to install or locate a toolchain. Read that file, check
  your edit against what it expects, then syntax-check the file you changed and stop.
```

**Why this is not the change that already failed.** Suppressing the command when the runner was missing was measured *worse* on both models, because silence is an open-ended question. This doesn't suppress — it swaps an instruction the agent can't carry out for one it can, on the same file. That distinction is exactly what the laravel/phpspreadsheet pair isolates: identical broken harness (no `vendor/`, phpunit unavailable, composer blocked), **+10.5 turns vs −14.5**, and the only difference was that one payload put a readable file in front of the agent. Both the mechanism (post-last-edit tail, AUC 0.945) and the counter-proof (fluentd's tail 11→2 from a correct test path) point the same way.

**Where the goal actually stands, plainly:** Sonnet is at **−3.4% suite / −19.6% exploration-heavy**, not 25%. This change is untested against a cell — it needs the plan's §3 gates (offline replay, Haiku do-no-harm, pre-registration, replicate) before it means anything.

Someone has already withdrawn that claim in `AGENTS.md`, and my symmetric cells independently confirm the call. Measured fairly, the tool is worth **−25.0% on Haiku**, roughly **−20% on Sonnet's exploration-heavy half**, and **~0% on Opus** — and the distance from there to 57% was prompt text, not the index.
